phrases.explanation: "And he will speak to people in his infancy and adulthood, and will be one of the righteous." Allah announces to you the glad tidings of a Word from Him, whose name is the Messiah Jesus the son of Mary, of high standing with Allah, and speaking to the people in the cradle. By "the cradle" He means the resting place of the child during its nursing. The exegetes differed over "and adulthood": others said its meaning is that he will speak to them when he appears as a grown man. Grammatically, "as a grown man" stands in the accusative, following the position of "and he will speak to the people." And "he is one of the righteous" means he is of their ranks and their close ones, because the people of righteousness belong to one another in religion and excellence, and he will speak to people both as an infant and as a grown man.

phrases.translation: Mary wondered, “My Lord! How can I have a child when no man has ever touched me?” An angel replied, “So will it be. Allah creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He simply tells it, ‘Be!’ And it is
phrases.explanation: When the angels told Mary that Allah gave her glad tidings of a word from Him, she said: "My Lord! How can I have a child when no man has ever touched me?" By what way could she have a child, whether by a husband and a man she weds, or whether Allah creates it within her without a man touching her. Then Allah said: "So will it be. Allah creates what He wills." That is, Allah creates from you a child without a human being touching you, as a sign for the people and a lesson. He grants the child to whom He wills, with or without a man, and withholds it from whom He wills. When He wills a thing, He simply says to it, "Be," and it is.

phrases.translation: And Allah will teach him writing and wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel
phrases.explanation: "And Allah will teach him writing and wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel." The reciters differed over the recitation of "and He will teach him." Most of the reciters of the Hijaz and Medina, and some of Kufa, read it with the third-person verb, "and He will teach him," patterning it after "Thus does Allah create what He wills" and "He only says to it: Be, and it is." The preferred judgment is that the two recitations do not differ in meaning, and with whichever of them the reciter recites, he is correct, because both convey the same meaning: a statement from Allah that He teaches Jesus the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel.

phrases.translation: and ˹make him˺ a messenger to the Children of Israel ˹to proclaim,˺ ‘I have come to you with a sign from
phrases.explanation: "And make him a messenger to the Children of Israel, to proclaim, ‘I have come to you with a sign from your Lord." "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord" means: We make him a messenger to the Children of Israel, with the fact that he is My prophet, My bearer of glad tidings, and My warner, and My proof of My truthfulness is that I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, a sign that confirms his word and verifies his report that he is a messenger of your Lord to you, and that his claim to prophethood is true.

phrases.translation: your Lord: I will make for you a bird from
phrases.explanation: Your Lord said: "I will make for you a bird from..." After saying "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord," He clarified what that sign is and said: "that I shall fashion for you," namely the sign that follows in the verse. So the sign from his Lord is the fashioning out of clay that he describes next. The sentence continues into the following phrase about the clay bird, and together they form one sign: making a bird from clay and breathing life into it by Allah's permission, which he mentions in the very next words of the verse, so that the sign is fully described across these two phrases.

phrases.translation: clay, breathe into it, and it will become a ˹real˺ bird—by Allah’s
phrases.explanation: Clay, like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a real bird by Allah's Will. He means: I fashion for you out of clay the form of a bird, and then I breathe into it, so that it becomes a bird by the permission of Allah. The reciters differed: some read "the form of a bird" and "it becomes a bird" in the singular, others both in the plural. The preferred recitation is the plural in both cases together, because it agrees with the written text and the widespread recitation. The pronoun "it" in "I breathe into it" refers back to the clay that was fashioned.

phrases.translation: Will. I will heal the blind and the leper and raise the dead to life—by Allah’s Will. And I will prophesize what you eat and store in your
phrases.explanation: Allah's Will. I will heal the blind and the leper and raise the dead to life by Allah's Will. And I will prophesy what you eat and store in your houses. By "I heal" He means: I cure, as one says "Allah healed the sick person" when He cures him. The exegetes differed over "the one born blind": some said it is the one who does not see at night but sees by day, others the blind person whose mother bore him so, others simply the blind person, and others the one with weak, blinking eyes. Jesus' bringing the dead to life occurred through supplication to Allah: he supplicated for them and Allah answered him. By "I inform you of what you eat" He means what he did not see with his own eyes nor witness at the time they ate it, and by "what you store up" what they put away, hide, and do not eat. Someone might object: astrologers and soothsayers often report such things and get them right, so what proof is there in this? The answer is that the astrologer and soothsayer deduce through causes that lead to knowledge of it, but that was not so with Jesus and the prophets: he reported it precisely, without deduction or cunning, because Allah let him know it, with no prior basis. That is the distinction between the prophets' knowledge of the unseen and that of liars. The prophets come with proofs that cannot be attained by stratagem except from Allah. The exegetes also differed over the scope of "what you eat and what you store up in your houses": some took it generally, while others said it means only the table that descends upon you and what you store up of it. In all of these signs there is knowledge of the unseen given by Allah alone, since none of them could be learned by observation or experience. The healing of the one born blind and the leper, the raising of the dead, and the telling of what is eaten and hidden in houses are all matters of the unseen that Allah made known to him, and they are signs for the Children of Israel that he is a messenger from their Lord, sent to them with the truth, so that they may believe in him and follow what he brings.

phrases.translation: houses. Surely in this is a sign for you if you ˹truly˺ believe
phrases.explanation: Houses. Surely in this is a sign for you if you truly believe. By this He means: in my fashioning the bird out of clay by Allah's permission, in my healing the one born blind and the leper, in my bringing the dead to life, and in my informing you of what you eat and what you store up in your houses without calculation, astrology, or soothsaying, there is truly a lesson for you and matter for reflection, by which you know he is truthful as messenger of your Lord in the command and prohibition of Allah, if you are believers who believe in the proofs of Allah and His signs, acknowledge His oneness, and believe in Moses and the Torah he brought you.

phrases.translation: And I will confirm the Torah revealed before me and legalize some of what had been forbidden to you. I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so be mindful of Allah and obey me
phrases.explanation: "And I will confirm the Torah revealed before me and legalize some of what had been forbidden to you." By this He means: I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, and as a confirmer of what was before me of the Torah. "Confirming" is a state clause relating to "I have come to you," as shown by "what was before me of the Torah." "With a sign from your Lord" means with a proof and lesson by which you know my truthfulness. "So be mindful of Allah and obey me" means: fear Allah in what He commanded and forbade in the Book sent to Moses, fulfil His covenant, and obey me in believing what my Lord and your Lord sent me with. That is the straight path, with no crookedness.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is my Lord and your Lord. So worship Him ˹alone˺. This is the Straight Path.’”
phrases.explanation: "Surely Allah is my Lord and your Lord. So worship Him alone. This is the Straight Path." The reciters differed: the majority in the cities read "indeed Allah is my Lord and your Lord" with a kasra on "indeed" as a new statement, while some read a fatha, interpreting it as "namely that Allah is my Lord and your Lord," with "indeed" referring back to "the sign." The preferred reading is the kasra, which the reciters in the cities agree upon, for their consensus is binding proof and personal opinion may not be set against it. So worship Allah alone, for this is the straight path and the firm guidance.

phrases.translation: When Jesus sensed disbelief from his people, he asked, “Who will stand up with me for Allah?”
phrases.explanation: "When Jesus sensed disbelief from his people, he asked..." By "sensed" He means: when Jesus found and noticed disbelief among his people. "Sensing" means finding and noticing, not the destroying and killing meant by the word without the article, and not affection and tenderness, which the same word can also mean. So when Jesus perceived the disbelief of his people, he turned to his disciples and asked them who would stand up with him for Allah, seeking their help against those who disbelieved in him, for he needed helpers in calling people to the religion of his Lord, and he addressed them with a question to stir them to respond.

phrases.translation: The disciples replied,
phrases.explanation: "Who will stand up with me for Allah? The disciples replied..." By "for Allah" he means "with Allah," for it is the custom of the Arabs, when they join one thing to another and wish to speak of both together, sometimes to use "unto" in place of "with." The exegetes disagreed over why Jesus sought help from the disciples he asked: some gave one reason, and others said it was because those against whom he asked for help wished to kill him. It is said that he asked them to stand with him against those who disbelieved in him and sought to harm him, so that he called upon them to aid him in the religion of Allah, and the disciples answered his call.

phrases.translation: “We will stand up for Allah. We believe in Allah, so bear witness that we have submitted.”
phrases.explanation: "The disciples replied, ‘We will stand up for Allah. We believe in Allah, so bear witness that we have submitted.’" The exegetes differed over why the disciples were named as they were: some said for the whiteness of their clothing, others because they were fullers who whitened clothing, and others that they are the chosen ones of the prophets. The most plausible view is the whiteness of their clothing and their work as washers, and the word also means an intimate associate. They said: we believe in Allah, and bear witness, O Jesus, that we have submitted. This is a report that Islam is Allah's religion sent with Jesus and the prophets before him, not Christianity and not Judaism, and an acquittal of Jesus from those who followed Christianity, like the acquittal of Abraham from other religions. It is an argument from Allah for His Prophet against the delegation of Najran.

phrases.translation: ˹They prayed to Allah,˺ “Our Lord! We believe in Your revelations and follow the messenger, so count us among those who bear witness.”
phrases.explanation: The disciples prayed to Allah: "Our Lord! We believe in what You have sent down and we follow the Messenger, so count us among those who bear witness." They affirm belief in the revelations Allah sent down, they follow the Messenger Jesus, and they ask Allah to inscribe them among the witnesses, that is, among those who testify to the truth of what he brought them. This is the prayer of those who stood with Jesus and submitted to Allah with him, asking to be recorded among His believing servants who bear witness to His message and His prophet. Their prayer is a testimony of faith and obedience, offered after they stood with him against those who disbelieved.

phrases.translation: And the disbelievers made a plan ˹against Jesus˺, but Allah also planned—and Allah is the best of planners
phrases.explanation: "And the disbelievers made a plan against Jesus, but Allah also planned, and Allah is the best of planners." By "the disbelievers" He means those of the Children of Israel who disbelieved, the same ones in whom Jesus perceived disbelief. It is possible that the meaning of "Allah's planning against them" is His gradual luring of them on, so that the Book might reach its appointed term, as was explained regarding "Allah mocks them" in surah al-Baqara. In any case, Allah is the best of planners: His plan encompasses theirs, and He is the One whose planning prevails. Whatever they plotted against him, Allah's planning is better, and none can turn back His decree.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when Allah said, “O Jesus! I will take you and raise you up to Myself. I will deliver you from those who
phrases.explanation:
"Remember when Allah said, 'O Jesus! I will take you and raise you up to Myself. I will deliver you from those who disbelieve.'" Allah devised a plan against the people who sought to kill Jesus, alongside their disbelief in Allah and their denial of Jesus regarding what he brought from his Lord, when He said to him: "Indeed I shall take you to Myself and raise you up to Myself," and so He took him to Himself and raised him up to Himself.

People differed over the meaning of the "taking" mentioned here. Some said it is a taking by sleep, meaning: I cause you to sleep and raise you up while you sleep. Others said it is a taking of death. Had Allah already caused him to die, He would not cause him a second death, for He has told His servants that He creates, provides, causes to die, and brings back to life, as He said in surah al-Rum. The explanation of the verse is therefore: Allah said to Jesus, "O Jesus, indeed I take you from the earth, and raise you up to Myself, and purify you of those who disbelieve." By "purify you of those who disbelieve" He means: cleanse you and free you from whoever disbelieves in you and denied what you brought of truth, from the Jews and the other creeds besides them.

phrases.translation: disbelieve, and elevate your followers above the disbelievers until the Day of Judgment.
phrases.explanation: Elevate your followers above the disbelievers until the Day of Judgment. By this He means: I shall place those who followed you upon your way, your creed of Islam and its original natural disposition, above those who denied your prophethood and abandoned your way, from all the people of the creeds, those who declared what you brought to be a lie and turned away from acknowledging it. Thus I shall place your followers above them, dominating over them, until the Day of Resurrection. Others said the meaning is: I shall place those who followed you from among the Christians above the Jews. The elevation of his followers lasts until the Day of Resurrection, and on that day all return to Allah for judgment.

phrases.translation: Then to Me you will ˹all˺ return, and I will settle all your disputes
phrases.explanation: Then to Me you will all return, and I will settle all your disputes. By "then to Me is your return" He means: then to Allah, O you who differ concerning Jesus, is your return, that is, your destination on the Day of Resurrection. And "I shall judge between you" means: at that moment I shall judge between all of you in the matter of Jesus with truth, "concerning that wherein you differed" about his matter. So the judgment over their dispute about him belongs to Allah alone on the Day of Resurrection, and no one else will settle it. He will judge with justice, and every party will receive what it deserves.

phrases.translation: As for those who disbelieve, I will subject them to a severe punishment in this life and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers
phrases.explanation: "As for those who disbelieve, I will subject them to a severe punishment in this life and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers." By "those who disbelieved" He means those who denied your prophethood, O Jesus, opposed your community, rejected the truth you brought them, spoke falsehood about you, and ascribed you to something other than what you deserve, among the Jews, the Christians, and the other creeds. In this world He punishes them by killing, captivity, humiliation, and poverty, and in the Hereafter by the fire of hell, in which they will abide forever. And they will have no helpers: no one will ward off Allah's punishment from them, for He is the Almighty, the Lord of retribution.

phrases.translation: And as for those who believe and do good, they will be rewarded in full. And Allah does not like the wrongdoers.”
phrases.explanation: "And as for those who believe and do good, they will be rewarded in full. And Allah does not like the wrongdoers." By "those who believed and performed righteous deeds" He means those who believed in you, O Jesus: they affirmed you as truthful, acknowledged your prophethood and the truth you brought them from Him, professed submission to Allah with the religion with which He sent you, and acted according to the obligations He imposed through your tongue, the laws He prescribed, and the practices He instituted. These He will reward in full. And by "Allah does not love the wrongdoers" He means that Allah does not love whoever unjustly deprives another of a right due to him, or puts something in a place where it does not belong.

phrases.translation: We recite ˹all˺ this to you ˹O Prophet˺ as one of the signs and ˹as˺ a wise reminder
phrases.explanation: "We recite all this to you, O Prophet, as one of the signs and a wise reminder." By "that" He means these reports He communicated to His Prophet concerning Jesus and his mother Mary, her mother Hanna, Zachariah and his son John, and the disciples and the Jews. "We recite it to you" means We recite it by the tongue of Gabriel through revelation. "Of the signs" means of the lessons and proofs against the delegation of the Christians of Najran and the Jews who denied the truth. "The Reminder" means the Qur'an, and "wise" means possessing the wisdom that distinguishes the true from the false. The reminder is wise because it settles the dispute.

phrases.translation: Indeed, the example of Jesus in the sight of Allah
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, the example of Jesus in the sight of Allah is like that of Adam." By this He means: truly, the comparison of Jesus, with respect to My creation of him without a male procreator, is with Me as the comparison of Adam. Proclaim that, O Prophet, to the delegation of the Christians of Najran. The verse came down concerning them when their notables, among them the Sayyid and the Aqib, asked: every human being has a father, so how can Jesus have no father. Some of them claimed that he is God, and others that he is a son of God, so the verse sets the true likeness before them. Allah says to His Prophet: answer them with this comparison, for it is decisive against their claim about Jesus.

phrases.translation: is like that of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, “Be!” And he was
phrases.explanation: Like that of Adam. "He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be!' And he was." Allah created Adam from dust and said to him "Be," whereupon he came into being without a man and without a woman, and became flesh. So the creating of Jesus from his mother without a male procreator is no more astonishing than the creating of Adam without a man and without a woman. Likewise was the creating of Jesus: Allah commanded him to be, whereupon he was. As for the grammar: if someone asks how "He created him from dust" can follow "Adam," which is definite and takes no relative clause, the answer is that it is not a relative clause but an elucidation of the likeness Allah set forth.

phrases.translation: This is the truth from your Lord, so do not be one of those who doubt
phrases.explanation: "This is the truth from your Lord, so do not be one of those who doubt." By this He means: what I have informed you concerning the account of Jesus, and that his likeness is as the likeness of Adam, whom Allah created from dust and to whom his Lord then said "Be," is the truth from your Lord, the account that comes from your Lord. "So do not be of those who doubt" means: do not be of those who doubt that it is so, for the example of Adam proves that Allah creates without a male procreator whenever He wills. So hold fast to what comes from your Lord and do not doubt it.

phrases.translation: Now, whoever disputes with you ˹O Prophet˺ concerning Jesus after full knowledge has come to you, say, “Come! Let us gather our children and your children, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves—then let us sincerely invoke Allah’s curse upon the liars.”
phrases.explanation: "Now, whoever disputes with you, O Prophet, concerning Jesus after full knowledge has come to you..." By "whoever disputes with you concerning him" He means: whoever disputes with you, O Prophet, concerning the Messiah Jesus the son of Mary. By "after the knowledge has come to you" He means: after the knowledge has come to you that I have clarified to you concerning Jesus, namely that he is a servant of Allah. Then He says: "Say, 'Come! Let us gather our children and your children, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us sincerely invoke Allah's curse upon the liars.'" By "let us pray earnestly" He means: let us curse one another, so that the curse of Allah falls upon whoever of the two parties lies about the matter of Jesus.

phrases.translation: Certainly, this is the true narrative, and there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Allah. And indeed, Allah ˹alone˺ is the Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: "Certainly, this is the true narrative, and there is no god except Allah. And indeed, Allah alone is the Almighty, All-Wise." By "this" He means what He informed you, O Prophet, concerning Jesus, namely that he is His servant and messenger and His word cast to Mary and a spirit from Him. This is the true narrative, so know that. And the creatures have no god with a claim to their worship except the God you worship, Allah. By "the Almighty" He means the Almighty in His vengeance against whoever disobeys Him, claims another god alongside Him, or worships a lord besides Him. By "the All-Wise" He means wisdom in His governance, into which no weakness penetrates.

phrases.translation: If they turn away, then surely Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of the corruptors
phrases.explanation: "If they turn away, then surely Allah has perfect knowledge of the corruptors." By "if they turn away" He means: if these who disputed with you concerning Jesus turn away from the truth that has come to you from your Lord concerning Jesus and the rest, from all the guidance and exposition Allah has given you, and do not accept it. By "Allah is All-Knowing of the corrupters" He means: Allah is the possessor of knowledge concerning those who disobey their Lord and deal upon His earth and in His lands with what He has forbidden them, and that is their corruption. So whoever turns away from the truth is among those whom Allah knows and will requite.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O People of the Book!
phrases.explanation: "Say, O Prophet, 'O People of the Book!'" By "the People of the Book" He means the people of the Torah and the Gospel together. The exegetes differed over whom this verse was sent down about: some said the Jews of the Children of Israel dwelling around the city of the Messenger of Allah, and others said the delegation of the Christians of Najran. The preferred view is that both groups are meant, because neither group has more right to it than the other, there is no indication singling out one to the exclusion of the other, and the name "People of the Book" applies to the people of the Torah and of the Gospel alike. Worshiping Allah alone is an obligation upon every creature that receives a command and a prohibition.

phrases.translation: Let us come to common terms: that we will worship none but Allah, associate none with Him, nor take one another as lords instead of Allah.”
phrases.explanation: "Let us come to common terms: that we will worship none but Allah, associate none with Him..." By "come" He means: draw near, from the root of loftiness, as one says "come to me." By "a common word" He means a word of justice between us and you: that we acknowledge Allah as One, worship nothing besides Him, and associate nothing with Him. The linguists differed over the grammar of "common": some read it as "even," others as a verbal noun in place of "being even," and it is also read as "just," from the root of justice, as in "an equal place" in surah Ta-Ha. A reported recitation has "to a word of justice between us and you." The exegetes differed over what the just word is: some said it is "There is no god but Allah." By "that we worship none but Allah" the particle stands in the genitive, meaning: come to the principle of worshipping none but Allah.

phrases.translation: But if they turn away, then say, “Bear witness that we have submitted ˹to Allah alone˺.”
phrases.explanation: Nor take one another as lords instead of Allah. But if they turn away, then say, "Bear witness that we have submitted to Allah alone." The exegetes differed over "take one another as lords": others said it means that some of them prostrate before others. By "if they turn away, then say: bear witness that we have submitted" He means: if those whom you call to the just word turn away from it and disbelieve, then say to them: bear witness that we, regarding what you turned away from, namely the oneness of Allah and pure servitude to Him with no partner, are Muslims, submissive to Allah with heart and tongue.

phrases.translation: O People of the Book! Why do you argue about Abraham, while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until long after him? Do you not understand
phrases.explanation: "O People of the Book! Why do you argue about Abraham, while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until long after him? Do you not understand?" By "O People of the Book" He means: O people of the Torah and the Gospel. By "why do you argue concerning Abraham" He means: why do you contend over Abraham, the intimate friend of the Most Merciful. The exegetes differed over the occasion: some said it concerned the claim of the Jews that Abraham belonged to them, others a similar claim of the Christians. By "Do you not understand" He means: do you not see the error of saying he was a Jew or a Christian, since Judaism and Christianity arose long after his passing?

phrases.translation: Here you are! You disputed about what you have ˹little˺ knowledge of, but why do you now argue about what you have no knowledge of? Allah knows and you do not know
phrases.explanation: "Here you are! You disputed about what you have little knowledge of, but why do you now argue about what you have no knowledge of? Allah knows and you do not know." By "Here you are" He means the people who said what they said about Abraham. By "you disputed about that of which you had knowledge" He means you quarreled about matters of your religion found in your books and brought by messengers, whose correctness was established with you. By "why do you dispute about that of which you have no knowledge" He means: why argue about Abraham's matter and religion, which you did not find in the books of Allah, which your prophets did not bring, and which you did not witness. Allah knows what is true, and you do not.

phrases.translation: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian;
phrases.explanation: "Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian." This is a refutation by Allah of the claim of those among the Jews and the Christians who disputed concerning Abraham and his creed and claimed that he adhered to their creed. It is an absolution of him from them, a declaration that they contradict his religion, and a pronouncement by Allah in favor of the people of Islam and the community of the Prophet, that they are the people of his religion, who follow his way and his ordinances, and not the adherents of the other creeds and religions. Thus the verse settles the dispute between them by declaring Abraham free of both claims and confirming the community of the Prophet as his true heirs.

phrases.translation: he submitted in all uprightness and was not a polytheist
phrases.explanation: "He submitted in all uprightness and was not a polytheist." By "upright" is meant a follower of the command of Allah and of His obedience, steadfast upon the way of guidance whose observance He commanded. By "submitting" is meant one who bows humbly with his heart before Allah, abases himself before Him with his limbs, and submits to the ordinances He imposed and made obligatory. And he was not among the polytheists who worship idols and false deities, or a creature alongside his Creator, who is the deity of creation and their Originator. The exegetes differed over the meaning of "the upright one," and the view closest to correctness was set forth earlier in this surah.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those who have the best claim to Abraham are his followers, this Prophet, and the believers. And Allah is the Guardian of those who believe
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, those who have the best claim to Abraham are his followers, this Prophet, and the believers. And Allah is the Guardian of those who believe." By "the people who stand nearest to Abraham" He means: those with the most right to Abraham, to standing by him and to the covenant with him. "His followers" are those who walked his way, acknowledged Allah as One, devoted religion sincerely to Him, made his manner their custom, and accepted his ordinances, upright and submitting without partners. "And this Prophet" means Muhammad, and "those who believe" means those who held Muhammad truthful in what he brought from Allah. "Allah is the Guardian of the believers" means Allah is their helper through Muhammad, against whoever opposes them among the other communities and religions.

phrases.translation: Some of the People of the Book wish to mislead you ˹believers˺. They mislead none but themselves, yet they fail to perceive it
phrases.explanation: "Some of the People of the Book wish to mislead you. They mislead none but themselves, yet they fail to perceive it." By "some" He means a community, and by "the People of the Book" the Jews of the Torah and the Christians of the Gospel. By "wish to mislead you" He means: they would like to turn you, O believers, away from Islam and bring you back to the disbelief they themselves are upon, and thereby destroy you. But "they mislead none but themselves": by trying to turn you from your religion they destroy none except themselves, their followers and adherents, for by this they brought down Allah's displeasure, wrath, and curse upon themselves, for their disbelief and breaking of the covenant in their Book about the Prophet. "Yet they fail to perceive it" means: without their perceiving or knowing it.

phrases.translation: O People of the Book! Why do you reject the signs of Allah while you bear witness ˹to their truth˺
phrases.explanation: "O People of the Book! Why do you reject the signs of Allah while you bear witness to their truth?" By "O People of the Book" He means the Jews and the Christians. By "why do you reject" He means: why do you deny "the signs of Allah", that is, what is in the Book of Allah which He sent down to you through your prophets, of His signs and proofs, "while you bear witness" that it is the truth from your Lord. So they reject what they themselves testify to be true, and the verse calls them to account for that contradiction. The verse reminds them that they themselves testify to the signs.

phrases.translation: O People of the Book! Why do you mix the truth
phrases.explanation: O People of the Book! Why do you mix the truth with falsehood? By this He means: O people of the Torah and the Gospel, why do you cloak the truth in falsehood. The meaning of "cloaking" was set forth earlier in this surah. The exegetes differed over what follows in the verse, and it is said that this concerns their conduct toward the truth they recognized. The verse addresses them as those who possess a Book, yet mix what is true with what is false in their treatment of what was sent down to the believers. They possess the Book, yet they conceal what it affirms.

phrases.translation: with falsehood and hide the truth knowingly
phrases.explanation: With falsehood, and hide the truth knowingly. By "and you conceal the truth" He means: why do you conceal the truth, O People of the Book. By "while you know" He means: while you know that what you conceal of the truth is truly true and comes from Allah. This is a report about the deliberate disbelief of the People of the Book in it, and about their concealing what they already knew of the prophethood of Muhammad, which they found in their Books and which their prophets brought to them, even though they recognized it. They recognized the prophethood of Muhammad in their own books, yet they hid it from others.

phrases.translation: A group among the People of the Book said ˹to one another˺, “Believe in what has been revealed to the believers in the morning and reject it in the evening, so they may abandon their faith
phrases.explanation: "A group among the People of the Book said, 'Believe in what has been revealed to the believers in the morning and reject it in the evening, so they may abandon their faith.'" By "a group of the People of the Book" He means the Jews who read the Torah. The exegetes differed over what this group urged: some said it was to outwardly affirm the Prophet without heart conviction and then deny it at day's end, and others said it was about the prayer, attending it at the start of the day and abandoning it at the end. The explanation is: affirm what Muhammad brought of the true religion at the first part of the day and reject it at the end of it, that perhaps the believers may turn back.

phrases.translation: And only believe those who follow your religion.”
phrases.explanation: "And only believe those who follow your religion." This is a report of the saying of the group of the People of the Book mentioned in the previous verse. By it He means: believe none except him who follows your religion and was thus a Jew. The exegetes differed over the explanation of the discourse. The most correct view is that the next words, "Say: verily, guidance is the guidance of Allah," are a parenthetical clause, while the rest proceeds in order: believe none except him who follows your religion, and do not believe that anyone is given the like of what you were given, or that anyone should dispute with you before your Lord on account of your faith, because you are more honorable in Allah's sight for what He favored you with. The verse refutes that saying: guidance is Allah's, and the bounty is in His hand.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Surely, ˹the only˺ true guidance is Allah’s guidance.” ˹They also said,˺ “Do not believe that someone will receive ˹revealed˺ knowledge similar to yours or argue against you before your Lord.”
phrases.explanation: "Say, O Prophet, 'Surely, the only true guidance is Allah's guidance.' They also said, 'Do not believe that someone will receive revealed knowledge similar to yours or argue against you before your Lord.'" The exegetes differed over the explanation. Grammatically, on one reading the whole discourse is a command from Allah to His Prophet to say it to the Jews, connected with no parenthetical clause, where the second "guidance" refers back to the first and "that" stands as its predicate. On another reading, "or that they should dispute with you" refers back to an omitted prohibition: believe none except him who follows your religion, lest you abandon the truth. The preferred view is the parenthetical reading, the most correct in meaning and the most orderly in structure.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Indeed, all bounty is in the Hands of Allah—He grants it to whoever He wills. And Allah is All-Bountiful, All-Knowing.”
phrases.explanation: "Say, O Prophet, 'Indeed, all bounty is in the Hands of Allah. He grants it to whoever He wills. And Allah is All-Bountiful, All-Knowing.'" By "verily, the bounty is in the hand of Allah" He means: verily, success in faith and guidance to Islam is in Allah's hand and with Him, not with you or the rest of the creatures. "He gives it to whom He wills" of His servants, as a refutation of their saying, "To none is given the like of what was given to you." That is not up to you, but only up to Allah, in whose hand are all things. By "All-Encompassing" He means the possessor of wide abundance with His bounty toward whom He wills to favor, and by "All-Knowing" He knows who is worthy of the bounty.

phrases.translation: He chooses whoever He wills to receive His mercy. And Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty
phrases.explanation: "He chooses whoever He wills to receive His mercy. And Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty." By "He singles out for His mercy whom He wills" He means: He grants His mercy singly to whom He wills, from the verb meaning "I singled out so-and-so with such-and-such." So His mercy goes to whom He wills, and none is singled out for it except by His choice. And "Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty" means He is the possessor of tremendous bounty, which He bestows upon whom He wills of His servants, and no one has a claim to it over another. His bounty is vast and encompasses all.

phrases.translation: There are some among the People of the Book who, if entrusted with a stack of gold, will readily return it.
phrases.explanation: "There are some among the People of the Book who, if entrusted with a stack of gold, will readily return it." Allah announces that among the People of the Book, who are the Jews of the Children of Israel, there are people of trustworthiness who return what is entrusted to them and do not betray it, and among them the betrayer of what is entrusted to him, the deceiver in his oath, who appropriates it as though it were lawful. If you, O Prophet, entrust such a one with a great quantity of wealth, he returns it to you and does not betray you in it. So among them are both the honest and the treacherous.

phrases.translation: Yet there are others who, if entrusted with a single coin, will not repay it unless you constantly demand it.
phrases.explanation: "Yet there are others who, if entrusted with a single coin, will not repay it unless you constantly demand it." If you entrust him with a single coin, he betrays you in it and does not return it unless you press upon him with demanding and exacting. Grammatically, the prepositions "with" and "over" interchange here, as one says "I passed by him" and "I passed over him." The exegetes differed over "unless you constantly demand it": some said it means unless you keep pressing upon him to demand it, others that it means unless you keep standing constantly over his head. The more sound view is the first: standing over him with exacting and demanding, because standing over the debtor's head does not necessarily make him desist, but demanding and litigating can recover the right.

phrases.translation: This is because they say, “We are not accountable for ˹exploiting˺ the Gentiles.”
phrases.explanation: "This is because they say, 'We are not accountable for exploiting the Gentiles.'" By this He means: whoever among the Jews regards betrayal as lawful and denies the rights the Arab has against him, so that he does not return what the Arab entrusted to him except while the latter demands and exacts it, does this because he says: there is no debt and no sin upon us in what we appropriate of the possessions of the Arabs, because they do not stand upon the truth and because they are polytheists. The exegetes differed over this explanation: some said what we have said, and others said something else.

phrases.translation: And ˹so˺ they attribute lies to Allah knowingly
phrases.explanation: "And so they attribute lies to Allah knowingly." By this He means: those among them who say "there is no blame upon us with respect to the possessions of the unlettered ones among the Arabs if we deceive them in it," through their claim that Allah has made that lawful for them, tell a lie against Allah deliberately, committing sin by uttering the lie against Allah, namely that He made that lawful for them. And that is what "while they know" means: they say it knowing that it is a lie, and knowing that the claim that Allah made it lawful is false. They know the truth, yet they ascribe to Allah what He did not permit.

phrases.translation: Absolutely! Those who honour their trusts and shun evil—surely Allah loves those who are mindful ˹of Him˺
phrases.explanation: "Absolutely! Those who honour their trusts and shun evil, surely Allah loves those who are mindful of Him." By "whoever fulfills his covenant" He means: whoever fulfills the covenant of Allah in His Book, believing in Muhammad and what he brought, returning trusts, and observing what Allah commands and forbids. By "and shuns evil" He means: who guards himself against disbelief and the sins Allah has forbidden, fearing His punishment. "Truly, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him" means Allah loves those who fear Him, avoid what He forbade, and obey what He commanded. The exegetes differed over the covenant, and the correct view was set forth earlier.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those who trade Allah’s covenant and their oaths for a fleeting gain
phrases.explanation: Indeed, those who trade Allah's covenant and their oaths for a fleeting gain. By this He means: those who take in exchange, by abandoning the covenant of Allah which He enjoined upon them, namely the covenant to follow Muhammad, hold him truthful, acknowledge him and what he brought from Allah, and by their lying oaths by which they make lawful for themselves what Allah forbade of the property of people entrusted to them, a contemptible price from the perishable goods of this worldly life and its paltry possessions. Such people sell their covenant and oaths for little, and the next phrase tells what they get in return.

phrases.translation: will have no share in the Hereafter. Allah will neither speak to them, nor look at them, nor purify them on the Day of Judgment. And they will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: They will have no share in the Hereafter. Allah will neither speak to them, nor look at them, nor purify them on the Day of Judgment. And they will suffer a painful punishment. By "no share in the Hereafter" He means: those who do that have no portion in the good things of the Hereafter and no share in the bliss of the Garden that Allah has prepared for its inhabitants, to the exclusion of others. "Allah will not speak to them, nor look at them" means He will not address them with mercy nor look upon them with favor. "Nor purify them" means He will not cleanse them from the defilement of their sins and their unbelief. "A painful punishment" means an agonizing chastisement. The exegetes differed over the occasion: some said certain rabbis among the Jews, others a particular man in a dispute.

phrases.translation: There are some among them who distort the Book with their tongues to make you think this ˹distortion˺ is from the Book—but it is not what the Book says. They say, “It is from Allah”—but it is not from Allah. And ˹so˺ they attribute lies to Allah knowingly
phrases.explanation: "There are some among them who distort the Book with their tongues..." By "them" He means the People of the Book, the Jews dwelling around the Messenger of Allah's city. By "a group who distort" He means a community that falsifies with its tongue the Book, so that you would think what they falsify in speech is part of the Book of Allah and His revelation. But what they twisted and invented is not part of the Book of Allah. They say, "It is from Allah," but what they twisted and invented belongs to no revelation of Allah. It is a fabrication about Allah, and they attribute lies to Allah knowingly.

phrases.translation: It is not appropriate for someone who Allah has blessed with the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood to say to people, “Worship me instead of Allah.”
phrases.explanation: "It is not appropriate for someone who Allah has blessed with the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood to say to people, 'Worship me instead of Allah.'" By "someone" He means any single human being, the collective noun for the children of Adam. "The Scripture" means the Book Allah sends down, "wisdom" the discernment He teaches. "To say 'Be my servants instead of Allah'" means to call people to worship of himself instead of Allah. When Allah gives a person the Book, wisdom, and prophethood, he only calls people to the knowledge of Allah, urging them to learn His precepts, and he is a leader in His obedience and worship, by teaching the people the Book and studying it.

phrases.translation: Rather, he would say, “Be devoted to the worship of your Lord ˹alone˺”—in
phrases.explanation: "Rather, he would say, 'Be devoted to the worship of your Lord alone.'" The word "but" introduces "be devoted to the Lord's worship," the preceding sentence making the saying itself unnecessary. The exegetes differed over "be devoted to the Lord": some said it means be sages and scholars, others the God-fearing sages, others the administrators and leaders of the people. The most correct view is that "devoted to the Lord" is a plural of one ascribed to "the Lord," the one who raises the people, sets their affairs in order, and shows care for them. One says of this: so-and-so raised my affair, and he raises it with a raising, and he is the raiser of it. When one intends exaggeration in praise, one says "rabbān," as one says "drowsy" from "he became drowsy." Most nouns on the form "faʿlān" come from verbs whose past has the form "faʿila," like "drunk" from "he became drunk," and "thirsty" from "he became thirsty." It can also come from the past form "faʿala yafʿulu," like "he became drowsy" and "he raises, he raised." So "be devoted to the Lord" means: be folk of reform and upbringing for the people through the Book of your Lord, devoted to Him in worship.

phrases.translation: accordance with what these prophets read in the Scripture and what they taught
phrases.explanation: "In accordance with what these prophets read in the Scripture and what they taught." The reciters differ over "because of what you taught of the Book and what you studied." Most of the reciters of the Hijaz and some of Basra read "because of what you knew of the Book," meaning your knowledge, study, and recitation of it. The general reciters of Kufa read "because of what you taught the people the Book," meaning your teaching the people the Book and your study of it. The most correct of the two recitations is "taught the Book," for Allah described the people as a pillar for the people in their religion and their world, folk who bring reform and upbringing for them. The most fitting explanation of the study is the reciting of the Book, for it is connected to "you taught the Book." The verse means: but be, O people, masters of the people and their leaders in their religion and world, through your teaching them the Book of Allah and what it contains of the permitted and forbidden, the obligatory and recommended, and through your recitation and study of it.

phrases.translation: And he would never ask you to take angels and prophets as lords. Would he ask you to disbelieve after you have submitted
phrases.explanation: "And he would never ask you to take angels and prophets as lords. Would he ask you to disbelieve after you have submitted?" The reciters differed over "and he does not command you": some read it with "then he would say to the people," while the preferred reading connects it with what precedes: it does not befit a human being that Allah gives him the Book, wisdom, and prophethood, and that he should say, "Be my servants besides Allah." The verse came down about people who asked the Messenger whether he wanted them to worship him. Allah showed that His Prophet calls people not to worship of himself but to be godly scholars. "Would he command you to disbelief after you have submitted" denies that he would command denial of Allah's oneness after your submission.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when Allah made a covenant with the prophets, ˹saying,˺
phrases.explanation: "Remember when Allah made a covenant with the prophets." The covenant of the prophets is what they bound themselves to concerning obedience to Allah in what He commanded and forbade them.  The reciters differed over the reading of "whatever I have given you": most of the Hijaz and Iraq read it with a fatha on the "lām" of "whatever," some reading "I have given you" in the singular and others in the plural, while some of Kufa read it with a kasra.  The correct of the two readings is "whatever I have given you," with a fatha on the "lām," for Allah took the covenant of all the prophets to confirm every messenger He sent, with whatever He sent him with.

phrases.translation: “Now that I have given you the Book and wisdom, if there comes to you a messenger confirming what you have, you must believe in him and support him.”
phrases.explanation: "Now that I have given you the Book and wisdom, if there comes to you a messenger confirming what you have, you must believe in him and support him."  The exegetes differed over whose covenant was taken: some said Allah took the covenant only of the People of the Book, not of their prophets, arguing from the words "you must believe in him and support him," for it is only the communities sent a messenger that are commanded to believe in Allah's messengers and aid them. Others said the covenant was taken of the prophets themselves, not their communities, that they would confirm one another and convey Allah's Scripture and messages. Others said it means the covenant of the prophets and their communities, the mention of the prophets sufficing for the mention of their communities, since in the taking of the covenant of the followed lies an indication that it was taken from the followers too.  The correct view is that Allah took the covenant of His prophets that they would confirm one another, and that the prophets also took the covenant of their communities and followers in the manner their Lord took from them, namely the confirmation of Allah's messengers, for they were sent to call Allah's servants to the obedience to which they themselves were commanded.  They also differed over who is meant by "a messenger confirming what you have": some said the prophets, whose covenants were taken that they would confirm one another, others said the People of the Book, who were commanded to confirm the Prophet when Allah sent him and their covenant to that effect was taken in their books.  The correct interpretation is that all of this is a report from Allah concerning His prophets, that He took their covenant to that effect and imposed on them the duty of calling their communities to it. So: remember, O People of the Book, when Allah took the covenant of the prophets, whatever I have given you, O prophets, of Scripture and wisdom, and thereafter a messenger from Me comes to you confirming what you possess, you shall surely believe in him and you shall surely aid him. And the messenger spoken of is the one described in the Scripture that is with you.

phrases.translation: He added, “Do you affirm this covenant and accept this commitment?” They said, “Yes, we do.” Allah said, “Then bear witness, and I too am a Witness.”
phrases.explanation: "He added, 'Do you affirm this covenant and accept this commitment?' They said, 'Yes, we do.' Allah said, 'Then bear witness, and I too am a Witness.'" "Do you affirm" means: have you affirmed the covenant you bound yourselves to before Me, that when a messenger from Me comes confirming what you possess, you shall surely believe in him and aid him. "The taking" here means acceptance and affirmation, as when the ruler takes a pledge of allegiance. "They said: Yes, we do" means: the prophets affirmed belief in Allah's messengers and aiding them. "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses" means: bear witness, O prophets, of the confirmation of My messengers and their aiding, against yourselves and your followers, and I am with you among the witnesses.

phrases.translation: Whoever turns back after this, they will be the rebellious
phrases.explanation: "Whoever turns back after this, they will be the rebellious." By this He means: whoever turns away from belief in My messengers and from supporting them, does not believe in that, gives no support, and breaks his covenant after the covenant Allah took from him, they are the corrupt ones, those who depart from the religion of Allah and from obedience to their Lord. These verses intend the Jews of the Children of Israel dwelling around the Prophet's city: what Allah held due from them of the covenant concerning belief in the prophethood of Muhammad, reminding them of the compacts of their fathers and of his description and mark in the Books of Allah.

phrases.translation: Do they desire a way other than Allah’s—knowing
phrases.explanation: "Do they then seek other than the religion of Allah." The reciters differ over this: most of the reciters of the Hijaz and Kufa read "do you seek" and "you are returned" in the second person, some of the Hijaz read both in the third person, and some of Basra read "they seek" in the third person but "you are returned" in the second.  The most correct is the second-person reading, for the verses before this are an address directed to them, and joining the address to its like is better than turning the discourse toward what is not its like.  Meaning: do you, O community of the People of the Book, then seek and desire other than obedience to Allah.

phrases.translation: that all those in the heavens and the earth submit to His Will, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will ˹all˺ be returned
phrases.explanation: "While to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and to Him they will be returned." To Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, through servitude, acknowledging that Lordship belongs to Him alone, and through the pure profession of His oneness and divinity. "Willingly" means whoever submitted willingly, such as the angels, the prophets, and the messengers. "Unwillingly" means whoever among them was unwilling, and the exegetes differed over the manner of that unwilling submission: some said it is his acknowledgment that Allah is his Creator and Lord even though he ascribes a partner to Him in worship, others that it was at the moment the covenant was taken from him, others the prostrating of his shadow, others submission of the heart to Allah's will even though he denies His divinity with his tongue, others submission out of fear of the sword, and others that the unbeliever submitted at the moment of death, when submission no longer avails him. "And to Him they will be returned" means: to Him, O community of those who pursue a religion other than Islam, you return after your death, and He recompenses you according to your deeds, the doer of good according to his good and the doer of evil according to his evil.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac,
phrases.explanation: Say, O Prophet, 'We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac...' This answers the previous verse's question about desiring a religion other than that of Allah, which is omitted as evident. 'We believe in Allah' means: we have given belief to Allah, that He is our Lord and our God, that there is no god but Him, and we worship none besides Him. 'And in what has been revealed to us' means: and we have given belief to what was sent down to us of His revelation. 'And in what was revealed to Abraham' means: and to what was sent down to Abraham, the intimate friend of Allah, and his two sons Ishmael and Isaac.

phrases.translation: Jacob, and his descendants; and what was given to Moses, Jesus, and other prophets from their Lord—we make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we ˹fully˺ submit.”
phrases.explanation: Jacob, and his descendants, and what was given to Moses, Jesus, and other prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we fully submit. By "Jacob and the tribes" He means his grandson Jacob and the tribes, the twelve sons of Jacob. By "what was given to Moses, Jesus, and the prophets" He means the books and revelation sent to them. "We make no distinction between any of them" means: we do not affirm some and deny others, as the Jews and the Christians disbelieved in some of Allah's prophets and affirmed others. We believe in them all. "And to Him we are submitted" means: we profess submission to Allah alone, free of every other religion, obediently subject and humble in servitude to Him.

phrases.translation: Whoever seeks a way other than Islam, it will never be accepted from them, and in the Hereafter they will be among the losers
phrases.explanation: "Whoever seeks a way other than Islam, it will never be accepted from them, and in the Hereafter they will be among the losers." By this He means: whoever seeks a religion other than Islam in order to profess it, Allah will not accept it from him. "Among the losers" means those who have withheld from their own souls their share in Allah's mercy. It is transmitted that the adherents of every religious community claimed to be the Muslims when this came down, whereupon Allah commanded them to perform the pilgrimage, if truthful, for pilgrimage belongs to the way of Islam, but they refused, and thus Allah refuted their claim. Others gave another explanation of the occasion.

phrases.translation: How will Allah guide a people who chose to disbelieve after they had believed, acknowledged the Messenger to be true, and received clear proofs? For Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people
phrases.explanation: "How will Allah guide a people who chose to disbelieve after they had believed, acknowledged the Messenger to be true, and received clear proofs? For Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people." The exegetes differed over whom this was sent down about: some said it concerned a man of the Ansar who apostatized after his Islam, others said it meant the People of the Book, and the more consistent with the apparent meaning is the People of the Book, though the narrations with the other opinion are more numerous. "How would Allah guide" means: how would Allah guide a people who denied the prophethood of the Prophet after affirming him, bearing witness that he was truly the Messenger, and receiving the clear proofs. "Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people" means: He does not grant guidance to those who exchanged the truth for falsehood and preferred disbelief over belief.

phrases.translation: Their reward is that they will be condemned by Allah, the angels, and all of humanity
phrases.explanation: "Their reward is that they will be condemned by Allah, the angels, and all of humanity." These are those who became unbelievers after their belief and after bearing witness that the Messenger is truthful. "Their reward" is the recompense for the work they performed. "Upon them rests the curse of Allah" means removal and banishment from Allah befall them, and the calling down of punishment upon them by the angels and by all mankind, all together, not merely a part of them. Allah made this the reward for their work because their work was disbelief toward Allah, so the curse and the harm of punishment reach all of them.

phrases.translation: They will be in Hell forever. Their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be delayed ˹from it˺
phrases.explanation: "They will be in Hell forever. Their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be delayed from it." "Abiding eternally therein" means remaining in the punishment of Allah. "The punishment will not be lightened for them" is a notification from Allah of the everlasting perpetuity of the punishment forever, without a fixed term and without any lightening at all. "Nor will they be granted reprieve" means no regard will be given to them for any excuse they might put forward, nor will they be delayed from it even for a moment. All of this is the very essence of the eternal abiding in the punishment in the Hereafter.

phrases.translation: As for those who repent afterwards and mend their ways, then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: "As for those who repent afterwards and mend their ways, then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful." Allah made an exception for those who repented among those who became disbelievers after their faith. "Except those who repented thereafter and did right" means those who repented after their apostasy from their faith, returned to faith in Allah and in His Messenger, and acknowledged as true what their Prophet brought them from their Lord, and performed good deeds. "Then indeed Allah is forgiving, merciful" means: toward whoever does that after his disbelief, Allah covers his sin, namely the apostasy, withholds the punishment for it and its exposure on the Day of Resurrection, without calling him to account for it when he dies in repentance from it, and shows him mercy with compassion.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve after having believed then increase in disbelief, their repentance will never be accepted. It is they who are astray
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, those who disbelieve after having believed then increase in disbelief, their repentance will never be accepted. It is they who are astray." The exegetes differed: some said it means those who disbelieved in some prophets sent before the Prophet and then increased in disbelief in him, so their repentance will not be accepted at death. Others said it means the People of the Book who disbelieved in the Prophet after believing in their prophets and then increased in sins, so their repentance is not accepted while they persist. The most correct is that it refers to the Jews who disbelieved in the Prophet after believing in him before his sending. "And it is they who are astray" means they abandoned the path of truth out of blindness.

phrases.translation: Indeed, if each of those who disbelieve then die as disbelievers were to offer a ransom of enough gold to fill the whole world, it would never be accepted from them. It is they who will suffer a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, if each of those who disbelieve then die as disbelievers were to offer a ransom of enough gold to fill the whole world, it would never be accepted from them. It is they who will suffer a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers." "Those who disbelieve" means those who denied the prophethood of the Prophet and did not hold him truthful, from every religious community. "And die while they are disbelievers" means they died in that state of denial. "From none of them will an earth-full of gold be accepted, even as a ransom" means no recompense or bribe will be accepted from whoever is in this condition in the Hereafter, even with gold enough to fill the earth, for a bribe is accepted only by one who needs it.

phrases.translation: You will never achieve righteousness until you donate some of what you cherish. And whatever you give is certainly well known to Allah
phrases.explanation: "You will never achieve righteousness until you donate some of what you cherish. And whatever you give is certainly well known to Allah." You will not obtain, O believers, the piety that is the goodness of Allah which you seek through obedience and worship, namely His favor in admitting you into His paradise and turning His punishment away from you. You will not attain the paradise of your Lord until you spend from that which you love, of your most precious possessions. "And whatever you spend, indeed Allah knows of it" means: whatever you give as charity, whether in the way of Allah or otherwise, none of it escapes Allah, until He gives the one who gave it his recompense for it in the Hereafter.

phrases.translation: All food was lawful for the children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed. Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Bring the Torah and read it, if your claims are true.”
phrases.explanation: "All food was lawful for the children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed. Say, 'Bring the Torah and read it, if your claims are true.'" Allah had forbidden to the children of Israel, the descendants of Jacob son of Isaac son of Abraham, nothing of the foodstuffs before the Torah. Everything was lawful except what Jacob forbade to himself, which his descendants forbade in imitation of their father, without Allah forbidding it before the Torah. The exegetes differed: some said the Torah itself forbade what Israel had forbidden to himself because of their insolence, others said nothing of it was forbidden in the Torah but they forbade it themselves and ascribed the prohibition to Allah, and Allah declared them liars and told His Prophet to have them bring the Torah and recite it so their lie becomes clear, others said the father's prohibition bound the descendants. The most soundly grounded view is that all food was lawful before the Torah except what Israel forbade to himself, binding through their father, and then the Torah came and Allah forbade therein what He willed. They also differed over what Israel forbade to himself: some said the veins, others the flesh of camels and their milk, and the most soundly grounded is the veins and the flesh of camels, because the Jews hold unanimously to that prohibition to this day. Israel was reportedly afflicted with the sciatic nerve and vowed to forbid camel flesh and milk if cured. "Bring the Torah and recite it" means: tell the Jews who claim Allah forbade them the veins, camel flesh, and milk in the Torah to come with it and recite it, so their lie becomes clear. Allah thus informed His Prophet of their lie against Him as a proof against them.

phrases.translation: Then whoever still fabricates lies about Allah, they will be the ˹true˺ wrongdoers
phrases.explanation: "Then whoever still fabricates lies about Allah, they will be the true wrongdoers." He means: whoever lies against Allah, whether among the Muslims or among the Jews, after the Torah has come to you, you have recited it aloud, and found nothing in it of what you claimed, namely that Allah forbade the veins and the flesh of camels and their milk. "These are the wrongdoers" means these who do that are the unbelievers who utter falsehood concerning Allah. Wrongdoing is placing something in a place other than where it belongs, and these are the very ones who did that with their false claim about Allah in this matter.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Allah has declared the truth. So follow the Way of Abraham, the upright—who was not a polytheist.”
phrases.explanation: "Say, 'Allah has declared the truth. So follow the Way of Abraham, the upright, who was not a polytheist.'" "Say, O Prophet, 'Allah has spoken the truth'" in what He informed us, that all food was lawful for the children of Israel and that Allah did not forbid the veins, camel flesh, or their milk to Israel and his children. "Follow the Way of Abraham, the upright" means follow his religion of pure devotion to Allah alone. "And he was not among the polytheists" means he assigned no partner in worship and did not belong to their number or allies, for the polytheists reinforce one another in unbelief. So too you, O Jews, do not take another as lords besides Allah, and you, O idolaters, do not worship anything besides Allah.

phrases.translation: Surely the first House ˹of worship˺ established for humanity is the one at Bakkah—a blessed sanctuary and a guide for ˹all˺ people
phrases.explanation: "Surely the first House of worship established for humanity is the one at Bakkah, a blessed sanctuary and a guide for all people." The exegetes differed over "the first House": some said it was the first house of worship established for mankind, others that it was created before all the lands, which were then spread out beneath it, others that the place of the Kaaba is the place of the first house Allah established on earth. The correct view is what Allah said: the first blessed house and a guidance established for mankind is the one at Bakkah, that is, the first House established for mankind for the worship of Allah therein, blessed and a guidance, a refuge for the devotion of the devout and the circling of those who circle in glorification of Allah and in honoring Him. A sound report from the Messenger of Allah makes clear that the Sacred Mosque is the first house Allah established on earth. Whether another house stood on its place before is a disagreement addressed elsewhere. "At Bakkah, blessed" means the House located in the place where people throng together in their circling during pilgrimage and lesser pilgrimage. The origin of "Bakkah" is thronging: one says so-and-so thronged so-and-so when he pressed against him and jostled him, and the place was named after the action of those who throng together therein. "The first house" is in the accusative as a description of "the one at Bakkah," and "a guidance" stands in conjunction with "blessed" as another such description of it.

phrases.translation: In it are clear signs and the standing-place of Abraham. Whoever enters it should be safe.
phrases.explanation: "In it are clear signs and the standing-place of Abraham. Whoever enters it should be safe." The reciters differed over "clear signs": the reciters of the metropolises read the plural, while another read the singular, "a clear sign," meaning by it the standing-place of Abraham, one sign. The plural is the correct reading, on account of the consensus of the reciters of the Muslim metropolises. The exegetes differed over what the clear signs are: some said the standing-place of Abraham and the sacred precinct and the like, others the standing-place of Abraham and that whoever enters it is safe, others said the clear signs are just the standing-place alone. The correct is that the standing-place of Abraham is among the clear signs, and among the signs are also the Black Stone and the adjoining enclosure. The standing-place is the well-known place, the trace of the foot of Abraham in the stone upon which he stood, a sign of the power of Allah and a trace of His intimate friend. For the first House established for mankind, blessed and a guidance for the worlds, is the one at Bakkah, in which are signs of the power of Allah and traces of His intimate friend Abraham. Over "whoever enters it should be safe" they also differed: some said it reports that whoever committed a crime in the days of ignorance and then took refuge in the House was not seized there, others that whoever enters it is safe from the Fire, and others that whoever enters it seeking protection is safe from what he sought protection from so long as he is in it, until he goes out. On account of the consensus of the early scholars, whoever committed his crime outside the sacred precinct and then took refuge in it is not seized therein. They differed only over how he is led out to be seized: some said by withholding the means of staying, such as food, drink, shelter, and trade, while others said by every possible means of leading out. But whoever commits an offense deserving a prescribed punishment inside it, the punishment is carried out upon him therein, of which there is no disagreement among the scholars. The meaning is thus: whoever enters it is safe so long as he is in it, and he comes to fear only after going out or being led out of it, for he is not then entering it and is not in it.

phrases.translation: Pilgrimage to this House is an obligation by Allah upon whoever is able among the people.
phrases.explanation: "Pilgrimage to this House is an obligation by Allah upon whoever is able among the people." It is an obligatory duty upon whoever among those held responsible is able to find the way to the pilgrimage to Allah's sacred House. The exegetes differed over what the way is: some said the provision and the mount, others the health. The correct is that it is according to one's capacity, for the way in Arabic is the road or path. Whoever finds a path to the pilgrimage without a preventer has the obligation upon him, and only performing it absolves him of it. "Whoever" clarifies upon which of the people the obligation rests, for it rests upon some and not all. The reciters also differed over "pilgrimage," with no distinction in meaning claimed.

phrases.translation: And whoever disbelieves, then surely Allah is not in need of ˹any of His˺ creation
phrases.explanation: "And whoever disbelieves, then surely Allah is not in need of any of His creation." He means: whoever denies the obligation of the pilgrimage which Allah imposed upon him and rejects it, surely Allah has no need of him, nor of his pilgrimage and his work, nor of the rest of His creatures among jinn and mankind. The exegetes differed: some said it means he does not believe he has a reward for his pilgrimage or a sin for omitting it, others that it means disbelief in Allah and the Last Day, others disbelief in the signs in the standing-place of Abraham, others that his disbelief is omitting it until he dies. The correct is that it means whoever denies the obligation and rejects its obligatoriness, for the verse follows the obligation of pilgrimage, and disbelief in what Allah imposed is disbelief in Allah, whose foundation is denial. Whoever denies it hopes no reward from performing the pilgrimage and regards no sin in omitting it. These explanations, though differently worded, are close in meaning.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O People of the Book! Why do you deny the revelations of Allah, when Allah is a Witness to what you do?”
phrases.explanation: "Say, 'O People of the Book! Why do you deny the revelations of Allah, when Allah is a Witness to what you do?'" He means: O assembly of the Jews and the rest of all those who claim the religion through the books Allah sent down, among those who disbelieved in the Prophet and denied his prophethood: why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah, that is, why do you deny the proofs He gave to the Prophet in your own books, established against you concerning his truthfulness and prophethood, while you know his truthfulness. Allah thus reported about them that they deliberately disbelieve with knowledge and awareness, while Allah is witness to what they do.

phrases.translation: Say, “O People of the Book! Why do you turn the believers away from the Way of Allah—striving to make it ˹appear˺ crooked, while you are witnesses ˹to its truth˺? And Allah is never unaware of what you do.”
phrases.explanation: "Say, 'O People of the Book! Why do you turn the believers away from the Way of Allah, striving to make it appear crooked, while you are witnesses to its truth? And Allah is never unaware of what you do.'" He means: O company of the Jews and others who profess to hold the books of Allah true: why do you turn away from the path of Allah, prescribed for His prophets and the people of faith, him who believes in Allah and His messenger, desiring crookedness for it. These verses are mentioned as coming down about a man of the Jews who sought to sow discord between two tribes after Islam. Allah rebuked him and commanded concord. One view says the path is the Prophet himself, but the narrations agree the path here is Islam. Allah is never unaware of what you do.

phrases.translation: O believers! If you were to yield to a group of those who were given the Scripture, they would turn you back from belief to disbelief
phrases.explanation: "O believers! If you were to yield to a group of those who were given the Scripture, they would turn you back from belief to disbelief." The exegetes differed over who was intended. The explanation is: O you who believed in Allah and His Messenger and acknowledged what their Prophet brought, if you obey a group of those who claim the Book among the people of the Torah and the Gospel and accept what they command you, they will lead you astray and turn you back as disbelievers, after your affirmation of your Lord's Messenger. Thus Allah forbade seeking their counsel or advice, and informed them that toward them they are full of malice, deceit, envy, and hatred.

phrases.translation: How can you disbelieve when Allah’s revelations are recited to you and His Messenger is in your midst? Whoever holds firmly to Allah is surely guided to the Straight Path
phrases.explanation: "How can you disbelieve when Allah's revelations are recited to you and His Messenger is in your midst? Whoever holds firmly to Allah is surely guided to the Straight Path." He means: how can you disbelieve, O you believers, after your faith in Allah and His Messenger, turning back upon your heels, while the verses of Allah are recited to you and His Messenger is among you, another proof against you, all calling you to the truth and forbidding error. What is your excuse before your Lord for denying your Prophet's prophethood, while with him are these clear proofs. The rope is called a holding-fast because it is the means by which one attains his need. "Guidance" and "the path" mean Islam. The dissension of two tribes was part of the occasion of this saying.

phrases.translation: O believers! Be mindful of Allah in the way He deserves, and do not die except in ˹a state of full˺ submission ˹to Him˺
phrases.explanation: "O believers! Be mindful of Allah in the way He deserves, and do not die except in a state of full submission to Him." He means: O community of those who truly affirmed Allah and His Messenger: fear Allah and watch over Him by obeying Him and avoiding disobedience, with the true fear of Him, which is that He be obeyed and not opposed, thanked and not treated with ingratitude, remembered and not forgotten. And do not die except as those submitted to your Lord, reserving divinity and worship exclusively for Him. The exegetes differed over "be mindful of Allah in the way He deserves": some said it is in force, not abrogated, others that it is abrogated by "so be mindful of Allah as much as you are able." "Do not die except in a state of full submission" means dying upon Islam.

phrases.translation: And hold firmly to the rope of Allah and do not be divided.
phrases.explanation: "And hold firmly to the rope of Allah and do not be divided."
