He means: cling, all of you together as one single group, to the means that lead to Allah, and hold fast to the religion of Allah which He commanded you and to His covenant which He made with you in His Book, namely concord and uniting upon the word of truth and full submission to His command. The rope is the means by which one attains what is needed, as safety is called a rope because it delivers one from fear and dread. The exegetes differed over "the rope": some said it is the Quran and the covenant made in it, others the pure profession of Allah's oneness. "And do not be divided" means: do not become divided away from the religion of Allah and His covenant, namely concord and uniting upon obedience to Him and His Messenger and adherence to His command.

phrases.translation: Remember Allah’s favour upon you when you were enemies, then He united your hearts, so you—by His grace—became brothers. And you were at the brink of a fiery pit and He saved you from it.
phrases.explanation: "Remember Allah's favour upon you when you were enemies, then He united your hearts, so you, by His grace, became brothers. And you were at the brink of a fiery pit and He saved you from it." "Remember the favour of Allah upon you" means remember the favor with which Allah favored you, namely concord and uniting upon Islam, for "when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together" is connected with it. So remember, O believers, Allah's favor when you were enemies in your ascribing of partners to Allah, some of you killing others out of tribal pride, and Allah through Islam brought your hearts together, making you brothers through the concord of Islam. The favor Allah commanded the helpers to remember is the concord of Islam and the agreement of their word upon it. The enmity was that of the wars between the two tribes, the Aws and the Khazraj, in the days of ignorance, until Allah extinguished it through His Prophet. "So that by His grace you became brothers" means through Allah's bringing-together through Islam you became sincere brothers with no rancor or envy. "And you were at the brink of a pit of the Fire" means you were on the brink of Hell through your disbelief before Allah favored you with Islam, and nothing stood between you and falling into it but dying upon that disbelief. Then Allah saved you from it through the faith to which He guided you.

phrases.translation: This is how Allah makes His revelations clear to you, so that you may be ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.explanation: "This is how Allah makes His revelations clear to you, so that you may be rightly guided." By "thus" He means: just as your Lord made clear to you, O believers, in these verses the rancor of the Jews which they conceal toward you, their deceit, His command and prohibition, your condition in your days of ignorance and what you have come to in your Islam, and the places of His favor and benefactions, likewise He makes clear to you the rest of His proofs in His revelation and upon the tongue of His Messenger.  "So that you may be rightly guided" means: so that you may be guided to the path of rectitude and walk upon it and not stray from it.

phrases.translation: Let there be a group among you who call ˹others˺ to goodness, encourage what is good, and forbid what is evil—it is they who will be successful
phrases.explanation: "Let there be a group among you who call others to goodness, encourage what is good, and forbid what is evil. It is they who will be successful."  He means: let there be among you, O believers, a community, that is a group, that calls the people to good, that is to Islam and its ordinances which Allah instituted for His servants, and enjoins what is right, that is, enjoins the people to follow the Prophet and his religion which he brought from Allah, and forbids what is wrong, that is, forbids disbelief in Allah and denial of the Prophet and of what he brought, by fighting them until they submit.  "And it is they who will be successful" means those who attain success with Allah, who abide in His gardens and His bliss.

phrases.translation: And do not be like those who split ˹into sects˺ and differed after clear proofs had come to them. It is they who will suffer a tremendous punishment
phrases.explanation: "And do not be like those who split into sects and differed after clear proofs had come to them. It is they who will suffer a tremendous punishment."  He means: do not be, O community of believers, like those among the People of the Book who became divided and differed concerning the religion of Allah, His command and prohibition, after the clear proofs came to them. They knew the truth but deliberately opposed it, went against Allah's command, and broke His covenant out of audacity toward Him. And for these who divided and differed after the proofs came them there is a tremendous punishment from Allah. So do not become divided in your religion as these became divided, and do not make their conduct a custom, lest that tremendous punishment befall you.

phrases.translation: On that Day some faces will be bright while others gloomy. To the gloomy-faced it will be said, “Did you disbelieve after having believed? So taste the punishment for your disbelief.”
phrases.explanation: "On that Day some faces will be bright while others gloomy. To the gloomy-faced it will be said, 'Did you disbelieve after having believed? So taste the punishment for your disbelief.'" By this He means: it is they who have a tremendous punishment on the Day when some faces become white and others black. As for those whose faces have become black, it shall be said to them: did you disbelieve after your belief, then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve. The "as for" requires an answer with "then," but when "then it is said" was omitted, the "then" dropped with it, which was permissible because the rest of the discourse indicates it. The exegetes differed over who is meant: some said the Muslims of the community, others everyone who disbelieved in Allah after the belief he professed when Allah brought forth the progeny of Adam and made them bear witness against themselves, others the hypocrites. The explanation is: did you deny Allah's oneness, His covenant, and His pledge that you would associate nothing with Him, after your affirmation of it. "Then taste the punishment" means for what you denied in the worldly life.

phrases.translation: As for the bright-faced, they will be in Allah’s mercy, where they will remain forever
phrases.explanation: "As for the bright-faced, they will be in Allah's mercy, where they will remain forever." Namely those who remained steadfast upon the covenant of Allah and His pact, who did not exchange their religion and did not turn back upon their heels after acknowledging the oneness of Allah and the testimony before their Lord that there is no god but Him. "They are in the mercy of Allah" means they abide in Allah's mercy, namely His paradise and its bliss and all that He has prepared therein for its dwellers. "They will remain forever" means they remain therein for all time, without end and without any limit.

phrases.translation: These are Allah’s revelations We recite to you ˹O Prophet˺ in truth. And Allah desires no injustice to ˹His˺ creation
phrases.explanation: "These are Allah's revelations We recite to you in truth. And Allah desires no injustice to His creation." "These are the signs of Allah" means the admonitions, lessons, and proofs of Allah concerning the affairs of the believers and the People of the Book, and those who exchange their religion. Allah recites these to His Prophet in truth, with truthfulness and certainty. Whomever He punishes, by blackening the faces and eternal tremendous punishment, and whomever He rewards, by whitening the faces and eternal bliss, this occurs without injustice toward either group, but with a right they deserved. "Allah desires no injustice for the worlds" means He places nothing outside its proper place, promising the people of faith and threatening the people of disobedience, as a warning to the former and glad tidings to the latter.

phrases.translation: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And to Allah ˹all˺ matters will be returned ˹for judgment˺
phrases.explanation: "To Allah alone belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And to Allah all matters will be returned for judgment." He punishes those who disbelieved after their belief with the mighty chastisement and rewards those who believe and remained steadfast with the eternal abode in His gardens, without wronging either group, for He has no need of wrongdoing, since the One to whom belongs all between the furthest reaches of the risings and settings has nothing deficient in His resources. "To Allah the matters are returned" means: to Allah returns the final outcome of the affair of all His creatures, the sincere and the corrupt, the doer of good and the doer of evil, so that He requites each according to what they deserve, without wronging any of them.

phrases.translation: You are the best community ever raised for humanity—you encourage good, forbid evil, and believe in Allah. Had the People of the Book believed, it would have been better for them. Some of them are faithful, but most are rebellious
phrases.explanation: "You were the best community brought forth for humanity, commanding good, forbidding evil, and believing in Allah. If the People of the Book had believed, it would have been better for them. Some of them are believers, but most are rebellious."  The exegetes differed over "you were the best community brought forth for humanity": some said they are those who emigrated with the Messenger from Mecca to Medina, others that you are the best community when you fulfill the conditions He described, others that they were the most responsive to Islam of all communities, and some linguists said it means the best community in the preserved tablet. The most fitting is that it is said when you fulfill those conditions. "You enjoin what is right" means you enjoin belief in Allah and His Messenger and acting according to His laws. "You forbid what is wrong" means you forbid ascribing partners to Allah, denying His Messenger, and acting against what He forbade. "You believe in Allah" means you believe in Him and devote pure worship to Him alone.  "If the People of the Book had believed, it would have been better for them" means: if the people of the Torah and the Gospel, the Jews and the Christians, held the Prophet and what he brought from Allah to be true, that would be better for them in their worldly affairs and their Hereafter. "Among them are believers" means among the People of the Book there are believers who held the Messenger true, and "most of them are transgressors" means those who departed from their religion, for it belongs to the religion of the Jews to follow the Torah and hold the Prophet true, and to the Christians to follow the Gospel, and in both Books is his description and mission, and both groups deny this, and that is their transgression.

phrases.translation: They can never inflict harm on you, except a little annoyance. But if they meet you in battle, they will flee and they will have no helpers
phrases.explanation: "They can never inflict harm on you, except a little annoyance. But if they meet you in battle, they will flee and they will have no helpers." "They will not harm you except with vexation" means: they will not harm you, O people of faith, these transgressors among the People of the Book, through their unbelief, except that they vex you by making you hear their unbelief and their call to error. "And if they fight you, they will turn their backs" means: if the Jews and the Christians fight you, they will be defeated and flee. "Then they will not be helped" means Allah will not help them against you, for He has cast terror into their hearts and supported you with victory, a promise of victory over the unbelievers.

phrases.translation: They will be stricken with disgrace wherever they go, unless they are protected by a covenant with Allah or a treaty with the people. They have invited the displeasure of Allah and have been branded with misery for rejecting Allah’s revelations and murdering ˹His˺ prophets unjustly. This is ˹a fair reward˺ for their disobedience and violations
phrases.explanation: "They will be stricken with disgrace wherever they are found, unless they maintain a bond with Allah and a bond with the people. And they have drawn upon themselves Allah's displeasure and poverty. That is because they reject Allah's signs, kill the prophets without right, disobey, and transgress." The passage explains that humiliation has been laid upon the Jews who deny the Prophet wherever they are, except with a bond from Allah and a bond from the people, namely a covenant already granted to them, securing them. The grammarians differed over the preposition in "except with a bond," and the sound view is that humiliation is imposed everywhere except the place of a protection. They returned with wrath from Allah and poverty as requital for rejecting His signs and killing the prophets without right.

phrases.translation: Yet they are not all alike: there are some among the People of the Book who are upright, who recite Allah’s revelations throughout the night, prostrating ˹in prayer˺
phrases.explanation: "Not all the People of the Book are alike. There is a group among them who stand, reciting Allah's revelations in the night and prostrating." The passage explains that humiliation has been imposed upon the Jews wherever they are found, except with a bond from Allah and a bond from the people, that is, a covenant and safe-conduct already granted to them, and they returned with wrath from Allah and poverty was imposed upon them for rejecting His signs and killing the prophets without right. The grammarians differed over whether the exception is connected or disconnected, and the sound view is that humiliation is imposed in every place except the place of a protection from Allah and from the people.

phrases.translation: They believe in Allah and the Last Day, encourage good and forbid evil, and race with one another in doing good. They are ˹truly˺ among the righteous
phrases.explanation: "They believe in Allah and the Last Day, command what is good, forbid what is evil, and race to do good deeds. It is they who are the righteous." The passage explains "They are not all alike": the believers among the People of the Book and the unbelievers among them are not equal, but differ in piety and corruption, in good and evil, and it was said only "not all alike" because it mentions the two groups, the believers and the transgressors among them. It is mentioned that the verses came down about a group of Jews who accepted Islam with a good Islam, among them those who believed and stood firm, and not the whole people perished, for Allah still had among them a remnant. The exegetes differed over "an upright community": some said it means a just one, others upright upon the Book of Allah, its obligations and limits, others obedient, and others that the People of the Book and the community of the Prophet, which is upright before Allah, are not alike in Allah's sight. The most correct is the view that "upright" means sincerely standing firm upon the guidance and the limits of Allah, steadfastly adhering to what He commanded and avoiding what He forbade, as in the parable of a people who boarded a ship. "An upright community" is in the nominative as a new sentence after "among the People of the Book," and a group of grammarians erred in taking it as an exposition of "alike," for omission of the second part is permitted only in expressions sufficient with one part. "They recite the signs of Allah during the hours of the night" means they read the Book of Allah in the hours of the night and ponder it, and "while they prostrate" means in prostration. The people differed over "hours of the night," some saying the hours of the night, whose singular is an hour of the night. The passage thus describes a group among the People of the Book that clings to the Book of Allah, holds fast to it, and is steadfast in acting according to it and according to what their Messenger instituted, reciting His signs at night and prostrating themselves in worship of Him.

phrases.translation: They will never be denied the reward for any good they have done. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of those mindful ˹of Him˺
phrases.explanation: "And whatever good they do, it will never be denied them. And Allah is All-Knowing of the God-fearing." The reciters differed: the reciters of Kufa read both verbs in the third person, reporting about the upright community, while those of Medina and the Hijaz read them in the second person, meaning whatever good you do, O believers. The correct reading is the third person. According to that reading, whatever good that community does, Allah will not deny it to them ungratefully, that is, He will not nullify the reward for that deed but will bestow on them abundantly the reward and honor. "Denying ungratefully" means covering over, and Allah is all-knowing of the God-fearing.

phrases.translation: Indeed, neither the wealth nor children of the disbelievers will be of any benefit to them against Allah. It is they who will be the residents of the Fire. They will be there forever
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, those who disbelieve, neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah. It is they who are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein forever." This is a threat from Allah at the corrupt faction among the People of the Book and at whoever disbelieved in Allah, His Messenger, and what He brought. "Those who disbelieve" means those who denied the prophethood of the Prophet. "Neither their possessions nor their children will avail them anything against Allah" means the wealth he amassed and the children he raised will avert nothing of Allah's punishment on the Day of Resurrection or in this world. They are the inhabitants of the Fire, abiding therein forever.

phrases.translation: The good they do in this worldly life is like the harvest of an evil people struck by a bitter wind, destroying it ˹completely˺. Allah never wronged them, but they wronged themselves
phrases.explanation: "The good they do in this worldly life is like a freezing wind that strikes the crops of a people who have wronged themselves and destroys them. And Allah has not wronged them, but they wrong themselves." The likeness of what the disbelievers spend seeking nearness to their Lord while denying Allah's oneness is as a wind with severe cold that destroys the crop of a people who hoped for its yield. Their reward is void. The exegetes differed over "the spending": some said spending as known, others a mere statement. "Allah did not wrong them" means He voided the reward of their deeds not out of injustice but because their deed was not for Allah, proceeding while they ascribed partners to Him. The unbeliever wrongs himself, earning through disobedience his place in Hell.

phrases.translation: O believers! Do not associate closely with others who would not miss a chance to harm you. Their only desire is to see you suffer. Their prejudice has become evident from what they say—and what their hearts hide is far worse. We have made Our revelations clear to you, if only you understood
phrases.explanation: "O believers! Do not associate closely with others besides yourselves. They spare no effort to harm you and wish you hardship. Hatred has already shown from their mouths, and what their hearts conceal is worse. We have made the signs clear to you, if you understand." "Do not take intimates from outside your own circle" means do not take allies from outside your religion, from anyone but the believers. The verse came down about Muslims who associated with Jews and hypocrites. "They spare no effort to corrupt you" means they refrain from no corrupting effort. "They wish for what harms you" means they wish your ruin. "Hatred has shown from their mouths" means their unbelief. "What their hearts conceal is worse." "We have made the signs clear to you" means the lessons from their affair.

phrases.translation: Here you are! You love them but they do not love you, and you believe in all Scriptures. When they meet you they say, “We believe.” But when alone, they bite their fingertips in rage. Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “˹May you˺ die of your rage!” Surely Allah knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart
phrases.explanation: "You love them, but they do not love you, and you believe in the whole Book. And when they meet you, they say, 'We believe,' but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips in rage. Say, 'Die in your rage.' Indeed, Allah knows what is in the hearts." "You love them, while they do not love you" means you, O believers, love these unbelievers whom Allah forbade you to take as confidants to the exclusion of the believers, while they conceal enmity and treachery toward you. "You believe in the whole Book" means in all the Books, yours and theirs and what preceded, while they reject and alter what is therein, so you are more entitled to enmity toward them than they toward you. The verse clarifies the mercy of the believers toward those who oppose them and the hardness of the hearts of the unbelievers. It came down concerning the hypocrites. "When they meet you, they say, 'We believe,' but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips out of rage" means those forbidden as confidants say "We believe" out of precaution and fear for their blood when they meet the believers, and when alone they bite their fingertips out of rage at the believers. "Say, 'Die in your rage'" is a command in the form of a supplication, that the Prophet supplicate against them that Allah cause them to perish from grief at their rage, before they see in the believers what they wish of affliction. "Allah is All-Knowing of what is in the breasts" means He knows what they conceal of hatred, greater than what their tongues showed.

phrases.translation: When you ˹believers˺ are touched with good, they grieve; but when you are afflicted with evil, they rejoice. ˹Yet,˺ if you are patient and mindful ˹of Allah˺, their schemes will not harm you in the least. Surely Allah is Fully Aware of what they do
phrases.explanation: "If good touches you, it grieves them, and if an evil befalls you, they rejoice. But if you are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah encompasses what they do." The passage explains the verse before it, about those who love the unbelievers while the unbelievers do not love them, who say "We believe" when meeting the believers but bite their fingertips in rage when alone, and to whom is said "Die in your rage," for Allah knows what is in the breasts. It clarifies that the believer loves the hypocrite and shows him mercy, and the believer is better to the hypocrite than the hypocrite is to the believer.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember, O Prophet,˺ when you left your home in the early morning to position the believers in the battlefield. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: "And when you set out in the morning from your family to assign the believers their positions for battle, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing." He means: if you are patient and God-fearing their cunning will harm you nothing, but Allah will aid you if you obey, just as He aided you at Badr while few. So remember when your Prophet set out to assign positions to the believers. The exegetes differed over the day meant, some saying Uhud, others the Confederates, and the most correct is Uhud, since the next verse's two groups about to lose heart were two tribes of the helpers, which happened only at Uhud. "Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing" means He hears what the believers said when consulted about where to meet the enemy, and knows the best opinion and what hearts conceal.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when two groups among you ˹believers˺ were about to cower, then Allah reassured them. So in Allah let the believers put their trust
phrases.explanation: "When two groups among you were about to lose heart, while Allah is their Protector, and upon Allah the believers should rely. And indeed Allah helped you at Badr when you were lowly. So fear Allah, that you may be grateful." The two groups about to lose heart were two tribes of the helpers on the day of Uhud, when their leader turned away with his people. Losing heart meant turning away out of cowardice, without doubt about Islam, and Allah preserved them from it. "While Allah is their Protector" means He defended them against that, and relying on Allah means trust in Him. "Allah helped you at Badr when you were lowly" means few, about three hundred and ten against nine hundred to a thousand, and He made you victorious. Today you are more numerous, so if patient He will help you as He helped you that day. "So fear Allah, that you may be grateful" means obey Him, that you may be grateful for His favor and the victory of your religion.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah made you victorious at Badr when you were ˹vastly˺ outnumbered. So be mindful of Allah, perhaps you will be grateful
phrases.explanation: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?" The passage explains that Allah helped you at Badr when you were few, when you asked whether three thousand angels would not suffice, and that was Badr. The exegetes differed over whether the angels were present: some said Allah promised reinforcement if the enemy came at once but they were not reinforced, others that they were steadfast and were reinforced, others the promise was for all wars if steadfast, steadfast only at the Confederates. The correct view is that Allah promised three thousand, then five thousand if steadfast, and the verse does not state whether they were sent. A raider was reported to wish to reinforce the polytheists at Badr, weighing on the Muslims.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember, O Prophet,˺ when you said to the believers, “Is it not enough that your Lord will send down a reinforcement of three thousand angels for your aid?”
phrases.explanation: "Yes, if you are steadfast and fear Allah, and they come upon you all at once, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand marked angels." The passage explains the promise made at Badr and Uhud: three thousand angels, then five thousand if steadfast and the enemy came at once. The exegetes differed over "at once": some said from their march, a raider coming at Badr to help the polytheists, others from their wrath at Uhud over their dead at Badr. They also differed over whether the believers were reinforced at Uhud: some said no, because the archers left their position for the spoils and were defeated. The Quran indicates a thousand angels at Badr, and at Uhud it is clearer they were not reinforced, since otherwise they would not have been defeated.

phrases.translation: Most certainly, if you ˹believers˺ are firm and mindful ˹of Allah˺ and the enemy launches a sudden attack on you, Allah will reinforce you with five thousand angels designated ˹for battle˺
phrases.explanation: "When you said to the believers, 'Is it not enough for you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?' Yes, if you are steadfast and fear Allah, and they come upon you at once, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand marked angels." The passage explains that Allah helped you at Badr when you were few and you asked whether three thousand angels would not suffice, and that was Badr. The exegetes differed over the occasion: some said Badr, when a raider wished to reinforce the polytheists, and the five thousand were conditional on the enemy coming at once, others said Uhud, when the believers asked if Allah would reinforce them as at Badr. They differed over whether the angels reinforced them. The sound view is that Allah promised three thousand, then five thousand on the conditions, without stating whether they were sent. The Quran indicates a thousand angels at Badr, and at Uhud it is clearer they were not reinforced, or they would not have been defeated.

phrases.translation: Allah ordained this ˹reinforcement˺ only as good news for you and reassurance for your hearts. And victory comes only from Allah—the Almighty, All-Wise—
phrases.explanation: "Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand marked angels." The reciters differed over "marked": most of Medina and Kufa read it as Allah marked them, while some of Kufa and Basra read it as the angels marked themselves. The correct reading is that the angels marked themselves, per the numerous reports. The marking was wool or dyed wool on the forelocks and tails of their horses, riding dappled horses, some saying they descended wearing yellow turbans like a well-known warrior's yellow turban at Badr. It is reported that the Prophet said: "Mark yourselves, for the angels have already marked themselves," and that the first use of wool as a mark was that day. Those reading it as Allah marked them said the mark of battle was upon them, ascribed to Allah.

phrases.translation: to destroy a group of the disbelievers and humble the rest, causing them to withdraw in disappointment
phrases.explanation: "To destroy a group of the disbelievers and humble the rest, causing them to withdraw in disappointment." The passage before it explains that Allah made His promise to reinforce you with angels only as glad tidings so that your hearts are set at rest by it. He means: Allah helped you at Badr that He might cut off a portion of the disbelievers, by "portion" meaning the group destroyed at Badr with the sword. Some said the verse means only those killed at Uhud. "Or humble them" means dishonor them with disappointment over the victory they hoped for, or cast them down upon their faces, so that they turn back disappointed. Victory comes only from Allah, the Almighty in retribution against disbelievers, and the All-Wise in what He ordains for you.

phrases.translation: You ˹O Prophet˺ have no say in the matter. It is up to Allah to turn to them in mercy or punish them, for indeed they are wrongdoers
phrases.explanation: "You ˹O Prophet˺ have no say in the matter. It is up to Allah to turn to them in mercy or punish them, for indeed they are wrongdoers." He means: He may cut off a portion of the disbelievers, or humble them, or forgive them, or punish them, for they are wrongdoers, and you have no say in the matter. "Or He turns in forgiveness" is accusative as coordination with "or He humbles them," though it could mean until He forgives them. The first reading is correct, for no creature's affair rests with anyone but the Creator. "You have no say" means to you, O Prophet, belongs nothing of My creation's affair except carrying out My command among them. It is said the verse came down when the Prophet, harmed at Uhud, despaired of them.

phrases.translation: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whoever He wills, and punishes whoever He wills. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: "To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whoever He wills, and punishes whoever He wills. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful." By this He means: you, O Prophet, have no authority at all in the matter. To Allah belongs all between the farthest reaches of the heavens and the earth, from where the sun rises to where it sets, apart from you and from them. He judges among them as He wills and pronounces the verdict that pleases Him, whether forgiveness toward whom He wills or punishment upon whom He wills, for they are wrongdoers, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful toward His believing servants.

phrases.translation: O believers! Do not consume interest, multiplying it many times over. And be mindful of Allah, so you may prosper
phrases.explanation: "O believers! Do not consume interest, multiplying it many times over. And be mindful of Allah, so you may prosper." He means: O you who believe in Allah and His Messenger, do not consume usury in your Islam after He guided you to it, as you consumed it in your time of ignorance. The practice then was that when a debt's term expired the creditor demanded it, and the debtor would say: defer my debt and I will give you more above the original amount. That is the usury multiplied manifold. "Be mindful of Allah, so you may prosper" means fear Allah in the matter of usury and in all He has commanded or forbidden, and obey Him, that you may prosper, escape His punishment, and attain what He urges you toward.

phrases.translation: Guard yourselves against the Fire prepared for the disbelievers
phrases.explanation: "Guard yourselves against the Fire prepared for the disbelievers." He says to the believers: guard yourselves against the Fire, lest you enter it through your consuming usury after I have forbidden it to you. It is the Fire I have prepared for whoever disbelieves in Me, so that you do not enter their entrance after your faith in Me, by transgressing My command. The warning is directed at the believers so that they abandon what leads to the Fire. He means: O you who believe, do not consume usury, multiplied manifold, as in your time of ignorance, when a debtor whose term had expired was told: defer my debt and I will give you more. Fear Allah in the matter of usury and in all He has commanded, that you may prosper.

phrases.translation: Obey Allah and the Messenger, so you may be shown mercy
phrases.explanation: "Obey Allah and the Messenger, so you may be shown mercy." The passage explains the verse before it: guard yourselves against the Fire prepared for the disbelievers, lest you enter it through your consuming usury after I have forbidden it to you. It is the Fire prepared for whoever disbelieves in Me, so that you do not enter their entrance after your faith in Me, by transgressing My command. The call to obey Allah and His Messenger and hope for His mercy follows the warning, so that the believer abandons what leads to the Fire and turns to obedience, and thereby attains the mercy and the garden prepared for those who fear Him.

phrases.translation: And hasten towards forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as vast as the heavens and the earth, prepared for those mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.explanation: "And hasten towards forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as vast as the heavens and the earth, prepared for those mindful of Allah." The passage before it explains that you should obey Allah in what He has forbidden, such as usury, and the Messenger in what he has commanded, that you may receive mercy, and it is said it rebukes those who left their posts at Uhud. "And hasten" means rush toward forgiveness from your Lord, what covers your sins out of His mercy, and toward a paradise whose breadth equals the heavens and the earth, transmitted as the seven heavens and earths joined. It is said the Prophet was asked where the Fire is if the paradise is so vast, and he said: this day, when it comes, where is the night?

phrases.translation: ˹They are˺ those who donate in prosperity and adversity, control their anger, and pardon others. And Allah loves the good-doers
phrases.explanation: "They are those who donate in prosperity and adversity, control their anger, and pardon others. And Allah loves the good-doers." He means: the Paradise whose breadth encompasses the heavens and the earth is prepared for the God-fearing, those who spend their possessions in the way of Allah, whether upon someone in need or to strengthen one too weak to rise for jihad. "In prosperity" means in joy with abundance and ease, and "adversity" means hardship and toil in livelihood. "Those who restrain their anger" means those who swallow their anger when full of it, withholding revenge. The origin is the filling of a waterskin, whence one full of grief is called so. "Those who pardon the people" and "Allah loves those who do good" complete the description.

phrases.translation: ˹They are˺ those who, upon committing an evil deed or wronging themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness and do not knowingly persist in sin—and who forgives sins except Allah
phrases.explanation: "They are those who, upon committing an evil deed or wronging themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness and do not knowingly persist in sin, and who forgives sins except Allah?" He means that the Paradise He described is prepared for the God-fearing, who spend in prosperity and adversity, and who, when they commit an indecency. "The indecency" is the abominable deed beyond what Allah has permitted, as of foul speech. Some said that here it means fornication. "Or wrong themselves" means disobedience that brought His punishment upon them. "Remember Allah" means they remember His threat, "ask forgiveness" means they ask Him to cover their sins, "who forgives sins except Allah" means who covers them except Allah, and "do not persist while they know" means they did not deliberately persist knowing Allah had forbidden it.

phrases.translation: Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and Gardens under which rivers flow, staying there forever. How excellent is the reward for those who work ˹righteousness˺
phrases.explanation: "Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and Gardens under which rivers flow, staying there forever. How excellent is the reward for those who work righteousness."  He means by "for them" those for whom He prepared the Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, the God-fearing He described. "Their reward" is their recompense for the deeds He described, "forgiveness from their Lord" being a remission from Allah of His punishment for their past sins, and recompense for their obedience. "Gardens beneath which rivers flow" means the rivers flow between their trees and at their feet, "wherein they shall abide eternally" means abiding forever in them, and "how excellent is the reward of those who act" means how excellent the recompense of those who act for Allah, namely these gardens.

phrases.translation: Similar situations came to pass before you, so travel throughout the land and see the fate of the deniers
phrases.explanation: "Similar situations came to pass before you, so travel throughout the land and see the fate of the deniers." The passage before it explains that for the God-fearing is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding forever. This verse means: already before you passed customary ways on My part among those before you, such as the people of Ad and Thamud, of Hud and of Lot, punishments upon the deniers of the prophets, for I granted them respite, led them to ruin, then sent My punishment. "Travel the land and see the fate of the deniers" means see the consequence of their denying My prophets, and know that the upper hand at Uhud is only a respite until their term, after which they turn to obedience or punishment hastens.

phrases.translation: This is an insight to humanity—a guide and a lesson to the God-fearing
phrases.explanation: "This is an insight to humanity, a guide and a lesson to the God-fearing." The passage before it explains the verse about the customary ways that passed before you: travel the land and see the fate of the deniers, for Allah granted the denying communities respite and then sent punishment upon them, leaving them as examples, and the upper hand of the polytheists at Uhud is only a respite until their term. This verse concludes that account: it is an insight to humanity, a guide for the believers, and a lesson for the God-fearing, who take heed of the fate of those who denied the prophets before them and remain firm in obedience and mindful of Allah.

phrases.translation: Do not falter or grieve, for you will have the upper hand, if you are ˹true˺ believers
phrases.explanation: "Do not falter or grieve, for you will have the upper hand, if you are true believers." This is a consolation from Allah to the companions of the Messenger for the wounds and slain at Uhud. "Do not falter" means do not become weak because of what befell you from your enemy at Uhud in slain and wounds, regarding the fighting against them. "And do not grieve" means do not sorrow or despair over the calamity that day, for you are the superior ones, those who prevail over them, and to you belongs the final outcome in victory, if you are believers, that is, if you believe your Prophet in what he promises you of the outcome of your affair and theirs.

phrases.translation: If you have suffered injuries ˹at Uḥud˺, they suffered similarly ˹at Badr˺. We alternate these days ˹of victory and defeat˺ among people so that Allah may reveal the ˹true˺ believers, choose martyrs from among you—and Allah does not like the wrongdoers—
phrases.explanation: "If you have suffered injuries at Uhud, they suffered similarly at Badr. We alternate these days of victory and defeat among people so that Allah may reveal the true believers, choose martyrs from among you, and Allah does not like the wrongdoers." The reciters differed over the word for injury: the general reading of the reciters of the Hijaz, Medina, and Basra is with a fatha on the qaf, meaning slaying and woundings afflicting you, then the enemy have already been afflicted by a like wound, while the general reading of Kufa is with a damma. The more correct is the fatha in both words, on account of the consensus of the exegetes that its meaning is slaying and woundings, though some philologists claimed the two are dialectal forms with one meaning, but what is known among the scholars of the language is what was said. "And those days We alternate among mankind" means the days of Badr and Uhud. "We alternate them" means We make them alternating turns among the Muslims and the polytheists: Allah granted the Muslims victory at Badr, killing seventy of the enemy and taking seventy captive, and granted the polytheists victory at Uhud, killing seventy of the Muslims besides the wounded. If there were no "and" in the sentence, "so that He may know" would connect to what precedes, but the "and" announces that a sought-after statement follows. "So that Allah may know those who believed" means so that He may distinguish the sincere believer from the hypocrite among you, the word carrying the sense of which, as in "which of the two parties," and the proper noun falls into the accusative when placed beside it. "And may take from among you martyrs" means so that He may honor with martyrdom whomever He willed. "And Allah does not like the wrongdoers" means those who wronged themselves through disobedience to their Lord.

phrases.translation: and distinguish the ˹true˺ believers and destroy the disbelievers
phrases.explanation: "And distinguish the true believers and destroy the disbelievers." The passage explains: "and that Allah may purify those who believe and may blot out the disbelievers."  "That Allah may purify those who believe" means that He would test those who believed in Allah and His Messenger by letting the polytheists gain the upper hand over them, until the sincere believer of sound faith is distinguished from the hypocrite. "And may blot out the disbelievers" means that He diminishes them and causes them to perish. It is said of so-and-so blotting out food when he diminishes it or causes it to perish, and from it comes the waning of the moon, its diminishing and disappearing.

phrases.translation: Do you think you will enter Paradise without Allah proving which of you ˹truly˺ struggled ˹for His cause˺ and patiently endured
phrases.explanation: "Do you think you will enter Paradise without Allah proving which of you truly struggled for His cause and patiently endured?" He means: or did you think, O companions of the Prophet, that you would enter Paradise and obtain your Lord's honorable reception while Allah has not yet made clear to His believing servants which of you is the striver in the way of Allah as He commanded. Its meaning was already expounded with proofs earlier. "And He has not yet established the patient" means those patient at the time of fighting, regarding what befalls them for Allah's sake in wounding, pain, and adversity. The word is read in the accusative, and it is transmitted that one reciter used to recite it in the jussive, connecting it with "while Allah has not yet established."

phrases.translation: You certainly wished ˹for the opportunity˺ for martyrdom before encountering it, now you have seen it with your own eyes
phrases.explanation: "You certainly wished for the opportunity for martyrdom before encountering it, now you have seen it with your own eyes." He means: you had certainly wished, O companions of the Messenger, for death, that is, the fighting, before you encountered it, and now you have seen what you wished for, while you were looking on, truly beheld before your eyes. Some grammarians said "while you were looking on" corroborates the statement, as one says "I saw him with my very eyes." It was said the verse was about companions who had not been at Badr and wished before Uhud for a day like Badr. When Uhud came, some fled while others stood firm and fulfilled what they had promised. Allah rebuked those who fled with this verse and praised those who were steadfast.

phrases.translation: Muḥammad is no more than a messenger; other messengers have gone before him. If he were to die or to be killed, would you regress into disbelief? Those who do so will not harm Allah whatsoever. And Allah will reward those who are grateful
phrases.explanation: "Muhammad is no more than a messenger" and "other messengers have gone before him". "If he were to die or to be killed, would you regress into disbelief?" "Those who do so will not harm Allah whatsoever." "And Allah will reward those who are grateful." He means: Muhammad is nothing but a messenger like those sent before him, who died when their terms ended, so he stands as they do. He rebuked the companions for the fear they showed when it was said at Uhud that Muhammad had been killed: "would you turn back on your heels" means would you apostatize after the truth became clear to you. "Whoever turns back" harms only himself, weakening not Allah's power. "Allah will reward the thankful" by steadfastness upon what Muhammad brought should he die or be killed. It came down concerning those who fled at Uhud when it spread that he had been killed.

phrases.translation: No soul can ever die without Allah’s Will at the destined time. Those who desire worldly gain, We will let them have it, and those who desire heavenly reward, We will grant it to them. And We will reward those who are grateful
phrases.explanation: "No soul can ever die without Allah's Will at the destined time. Those who desire worldly gain, We will let them have it, and those who desire heavenly reward, We will grant it to them. And We will reward those who are grateful." He means: no creature dies except after reaching the end of the life-term Allah has set, so when he reaches the written term and He permits it, he dies then, before that not through any schemer. The grammarians differed over the accusative of "as a fixed decree": some said corroboration, meaning Allah has written a fixed decree, others that the utterance conveys that He has written it. The correct view is that it is a verbal noun because of the meaning of what precedes. "Whoever desires the reward of this world" gets of the livelihood apportioned to him, with no share after that in the honor for the obedient, and "whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter" gets of Allah's honor. "We will reward the grateful" in the Hereafter for thanks for His favor.

phrases.translation: ˹Imagine˺ how many devotees fought along with their prophets and never faltered despite whatever ˹losses˺ they suffered in the cause of Allah, nor did they weaken or give in! Allah loves those who persevere
phrases.explanation: "Imagine how many devotees fought along with their prophets and never faltered despite whatever losses they suffered in the cause of Allah, nor did they weaken or give in. Allah loves those who persevere."  "And how many a prophet": the reciters differ, some reading it with a hamza on the alif and doubling of the ya, others with lengthening of the alif and lightening of the ya, two well-known readings and linguistic variants between which there is no difference in meaning, and with either a reciter has hit what is correct, its meaning being how many a prophet.  "Alongside whom many devout throngs fought": a group of the Hijaz and Basra read the verb as passive, was killed, and another of the Hijaz and Kufa read it active, fought. Those who read "fought" argued that had they been killed, "yet they did not weaken" would have no intelligible import, while those who read "was killed" said only the prophet and a portion of the devout were meant killed, and the not flinching was denied only of those who remained. "Al-ribbiyyun" stand in the nominative by "with him", a waw of circumstantial state being omitted, as one says "the commander was killed, with him a great army," meaning while with him was a great army. The linguists differ over it: some of Basra said worshippers of the Lord, singular ribbi, some of Kufa said the scholars and the thousands, others said the followers, and in judgement it is the many throngs, singular ribbi.  "Yet they did not weaken on account of what struck them on the way of Allah" means they were not rendered powerless by the pain of the wounds or the killing of some of them in the war against Allah's enemies, and did not recoil from their jihad. "And they did not slacken" means their strength did not weaken on account of the killing of their prophet. "And they did not submit" means they did not abase themselves before their enemy by entering his religion or flattering him out of fear, but went forward upon clear insight and their prophet's way, patient in Allah's command. "And Allah loves the patiently steadfast" means He loves these and those like them, patient in His command and in jihad against His enemy, not the one who fled, turned on his heels and abased himself because his prophet was killed, or was overcome by flinching and weakness.

phrases.translation: And all they said was, “Our Lord! Forgive our sins and excesses, make our steps firm, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people.”
phrases.explanation: "And all they said was, 'Our Lord! Forgive our sins and excesses, make our steps firm, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people.'" He means: the statement of the devout men was nothing other than this when their prophet was killed, they grasped at nothing other than patiently enduring what afflicted them, fighting their enemy, and asking for help. "Forgive us our sins and our excess" means the minor sins and our excess in them. "Make our feet firm" means stand firm against Your enemy. This is a reproof from Allah to His servants who fled at Uhud: why did you not act as these devout men did when their prophets were killed, standing firm and asking for help. For Allah loves whoever is patient in His command. The correct reading is the accusative.

phrases.translation: So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the excellent reward of the Hereafter. For Allah loves the good-doers
phrases.explanation: "So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the excellent reward of the Hereafter. For Allah loves the good-doers."  He means: Allah gave to those whom He described, namely patience in obedience to Allah after the killing of their prophets, struggle against their enemy, seeking Allah's help, and following their leader's ways in what they tested themselves for Allah, "the reward of this world," that is, a recompense in this world, namely victory over their enemy and the enemy of Allah, triumph, conquest, and establishment of their position in the lands. "And the most excellent reward of the Hereafter" means the best recompense of the Hereafter for the good works they sent ahead, namely the Garden and its felicity. "And Allah loves those who do good" completes the praise of those described.

phrases.translation: O believers! If you yield to the disbelievers, they will drag you back to disbelief—and you will become losers
phrases.explanation: "O believers! If you yield to the disbelievers, they will drag you back to disbelief, and you will become losers." He means: O you who have held Allah and His Messenger to be true regarding His promise, threat, command, and prohibition, "if you obey those who disbelieve," namely those who deny your Prophet among the Jews and the Christians, in what they command and forbid, accepting their counsel, "they will turn you back upon your heels," that is, bring you to apostasy after faith and to disbelief in Allah, His signs, and His Messenger after Islam, "so that you return as losers," that is, as the damned, having lost yourselves and your religion and your Hereafter. Thereby He forbids the believers from obeying the disbelievers in their opinions and following their counsel in their religions.

phrases.translation: But no! Allah is your Guardian, and He is the best Helper
phrases.explanation: "But no! Allah is your Guardian, and He is the best Helper." He means: it is Allah who keeps you upon the straight path, O believers, and guards you against obeying the disbelievers. It is said the verse says only "nay, Allah is your Protector" because in "if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back upon your heels" there lies a prohibition against obeying them, so it is as though He said: do not obey them, then began a new statement, "nay, Allah is your Protector," the name in the nominative though the accusative would also be correct. "Nay, Allah is your Protector" means your Ally and Helper against your enemies, "and He is the best of helpers," not those to whom you have fled, so seek refuge with Allah.

phrases.translation: We will cast horror into the hearts of the disbelievers for associating ˹false gods˺ with Allah—a practice He has never authorized. The Fire will be their home—what an evil place for the wrongdoers to stay
phrases.explanation: "We will cast horror into the hearts of the disbelievers for associating false gods with Allah, a practice He has never authorized. The Fire will be their home, what an evil place for the wrongdoers to stay." He means: Allah will cast into the hearts of those who disbelieved in their Lord and denied the Prophet's prophethood, namely those who fought you at Uhud, the terror and panic, because they ascribed partners to Allah, worshipping idols, for which He furnished no proof, the authority He did not send down. This is a promise of victory so long as you remain steadfast in obedience, for the setback at Uhud came from sins. "Their abode is the Fire" means their refuge on the Day of Resurrection is the Fire, an evil dwelling for the wrongdoers.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah fulfilled His promise to you when you ˹initially˺ swept them away by His Will, then your courage weakened and you disputed about the command and disobeyed, after Allah had brought victory within your reach. Some of you were after worldly gain while others desired a heavenly reward. He denied you victory over them as a test, yet He has pardoned you. And Allah is Gracious to the believers
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, Allah fulfilled His promise to you when you initially swept them away by His Will, then your courage weakened and you disputed about the command and disobeyed, after Allah had brought victory within your reach. Some of you were after worldly gain while others desired a heavenly reward. He denied you victory over them as a test, yet He has pardoned you. And Allah is Gracious to the believers."  "Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you" means the promise He made you at Uhud through the mouth of His Messenger, namely his word to the archers to remain at their place and not budge, and his promise of victory that day if they held to his command. "When you were slaying them by His permission" means when you killed them, by His decision and decree and His granting you power over them.  "Until you lost courage and disputed over the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love" means until you became cowardly and weak, differed over Allah's matter, and opposed your Prophet, abandoning his command, specifically the archers he had ordered to remain at their post at the mouth of the mountain pass facing the enemy cavalry, after Allah had shown you the victory and triumph over the polytheists, driving them from their women and possessions, before the archers left their posts and the cavalry broke upon the believers from behind. It is said the sentence is placed forward whose meaning is placing backward.  "Among you are those who desire the world" means those who abandoned their post and joined the camp craving plunder when they saw the polytheists' defeat, and "those who desire the hereafter" means the archers who held fast to their posts and followed his command, striving for Allah's reward. "Then He turned you away from them in order to test you" means He turned your faces from the polytheists because of your disobedience, as a punishment, in order to try you so the hypocrite is distinguished from the sincere believer. "And He has certainly pardoned you" means Allah pardoned those who opposed the Messenger's command, remitting their punishment though not destroying them, and "Allah is full of grace toward the believers" means He pardons believers much of what they deserve punishment for.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when you were running far away ˹in panic˺—not looking at anyone—while the Messenger was calling to you from behind! So Allah rewarded your disobedience with distress upon distress. Now, do not grieve over the victory you were denied or the injury you suffered. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do
phrases.explanation: "Remember when you were running far away in panic, not looking at anyone, while the Messenger was calling to you from behind. So Allah rewarded your disobedience with distress upon distress. Now, do not grieve over the victory you were denied or the injury you suffered. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do."  "When you were fleeing up the hill without looking back at anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind": He means He has surely forgiven you, O believers, when He did not annihilate you for your sins and flight. The reciters differed: the majority of the Hijaz, Iraq, and Syria read "you were fleeing" with a damma on the ta and kasra on the ayn, meaning hastening away and fleeing over flat terrain or into descents, which is the reading according to the consensus of the authoritative reciters, while one reciter read it with fatha on both, meaning climbing the mountain. The meaning of the preferred reading is that the people withdrew into the valley, for fleeing over flat terrain and in valley bottoms is that word, while climbing up takes place only on mountains and stairs. "Without looking back at anyone" means you did not look at one another fleeing, and "while the Messenger was calling you from behind" means he called you from behind, "To me, servants of Allah."  "Then He requited you with grief upon grief" means He requited your flight from your Prophet, your cowardice toward your enemy, and your disobedience, with grief upon grief, calling the punishment a requital because it was a recompense for an action He detested, grief after a grief that preceded it. The exegetes differed over the two griefs: some said the first was the report that their Prophet was killed and the second the killing and wounds, others the reverse, others that the first was the victory and spoils that eluded them and the second the enemy leader appearing above them in the pass.  "So that you would not grieve over what eluded you, nor over what befell you" means do not grieve over the victory and spoils you hoped to attain from your enemy, nor over the wounding and killing that befell you. "And Allah is well-informed of what you do" means He knows your fleeing, your defeat, your abandonment of your Prophet while he called you, and your sorrow, and He records all of it to requite the doer of good for good and the doer of evil for evil, or to pardon him.

phrases.translation: Then after distress, He sent down serenity in the form of drowsiness overcoming some of you, while others were disturbed by evil thoughts about Allah—the thoughts of ˹pre-Islamic˺ ignorance. They ask, “Do we have a say in the matter?” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “All matters are destined by Allah.” They conceal in their hearts what they do not reveal to you. They say ˹to themselves˺, “If we had any say in the matter, none of us would have come to die here.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Even if you were to remain in your homes, those among you who were destined to be killed would have met the same fate.” Through this, Allah tests what is within you and purifies what is in your hearts. And Allah knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart
phrases.explanation: "Then after distress, He sent down serenity in the form of drowsiness overcoming some of you, while others were disturbed by evil thoughts about Allah, the thoughts of pre-Islamic ignorance. They ask, 'Do we have a say in the matter?' Say, 'All matters are destined by Allah.' They conceal in their hearts what they do not reveal to you. They say to themselves, 'If we had any say in the matter, none of us would have come to die here.' Say, 'Even if you were to remain in your homes, those among you who were destined to be killed would have met the same fate.' Through this, Allah tests what is within you and purifies what is in your hearts. And Allah knows best what is hidden in the heart."  He means: after the grief that followed a grief, Allah sent down "a security," that is, safety, upon the sincere and convinced among you, not upon the people of hypocrisy and doubt, and clarified that the security was "a drowsiness" standing in the accusative as an apposition. The general readers of the Hijaz, Medina, Basra, and some of Kufa read the verb in the masculine, those of Kufa reading it in the feminine, the masculine assuming the drowsiness overcame the believers, the feminine assuming the security did. The cause of the two groups differing was that the one felt secure until it slept, while the other was concerned only with itself.  "And a group of you who were concerned only with themselves" means the hypocrites, who out of fear of death were preoccupied so that sleep fled their eyes, while they entertained about Allah false assumptions of the age of ignorance, doubting Allah's affair, denying His Prophet, and supposing the disbelievers would prevail. "The assumption of the age of ignorance" means the people of shirk. The nominative of "and a group" has two possibilities, by the pronoun in "who were concerned" or by "who entertained assumptions." They say: "We have no share at all in the affair." So He commanded His Prophet to say to them: "Indeed, the affair belongs entirely to Allah," He disposes of it as He wills, and had we any share we would not have gone forth to be killed. The readers differed: the general readers of the Hijaz and Iraq read "all of it" in the accusative as an apposition, some of Basra in the nominative, and the correct reading is the accusative by the agreement of the majority. They conceal in their hearts what they do not reveal to you.  Say: even if you had been in your houses, those for whom death was decreed would still have gone forth to the place of their fall, until struck down there. "So that Allah might test what is in your breasts" means so that He might put to the test the doubt in your breasts, so that He might distinguish you from the believers through what He discloses of your hypocrisy, and "purify what is in your hearts" means so that they might distinguish in your hearts conviction toward Allah and His Messenger, whether enmity or loyal allegiance. "And Allah is All-Knowing of what is hidden in the hearts" means He knows what is in the breasts.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those ˹believers˺ who fled on the day when the two armies met were made to slip by Satan because of their misdeeds. But Allah has pardoned them. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, those believers who fled on the day when the two armies met were made to slip by Satan because of their misdeeds. But Allah has pardoned them. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing." He means: those among the companions who turned away from the idolaters at Uhud and fled. "On the day the two hosts met" means the day the armies of the idolaters and the Muslims met at Uhud. "Satan only caused them to slip" means Satan summoned them to the sin. "On account of part of what they had earned" means part of the sins they had committed. "Allah has indeed pardoned them" means He refrained from punishing them and remitted it. "Allah is Forgiving" means He covers the sins of believers by remitting their punishment, and "Forbearing" means He is long-suffering and not hasty in vengeance. The exegetes differed over whom was meant: some said everyone who turned his back at Uhud, others only a specific group, namely those who returned to Medina.

phrases.translation: O believers! Do not be like the unfaithful who say about their brothers who travel throughout the land or engage in battle, “If they had stayed with us, they would not have died or been killed.” Allah makes such thinking a cause of agony in their hearts. It is Allah who gives life and causes death. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do
phrases.explanation: "O believers! Do not be like the unfaithful who say about their brothers who travel throughout the land or engage in battle, 'If they had stayed with us, they would not have died or been killed.' Allah makes such thinking a cause of agony in their hearts. It is Allah who gives life and causes death. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do."  He means: O you who held Allah and His Messenger to be truthful, be not like him who disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and said to his brethren among the disbelievers, "when these had journeyed through the land," that is, set out from their lands on a journey for trade, or "had been on a military campaign" and perished on their journey or were killed, "had they remained with us, they would not have died nor been killed." By this He reports their statement that had they remained they would not have died, so that Allah might make it a grief in their hearts, though life and death belong to Allah and lie in His hand. It is said those meant are a known hypocrite leader and his companions, others said all the hypocrites collectively. They differed over "journeyed through the land": some said trade, others said journeying in obedience to Allah and His Messenger.  "So that Allah might make that a remorse in their hearts" means grief in their hearts. "And Allah gives life and causes death" means Allah is the One who brings death for whom He wills and causes to die whom He wills, to the exclusion of all others. This exhorts the believers toward jihad and patience in fighting, teaches that life and death lie in His hand and none dies except after his written term, and forbids despairing over those killed in the war. "And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do" means He sees your good and evil and requites every doer according to what he deserves.

phrases.translation: Should you be martyred or die in the cause of Allah, then His forgiveness and mercy are far better than whatever ˹wealth˺ those ˹who stay behind˺ accumulate
phrases.explanation: "Should you be martyred or die in the cause of Allah, then His forgiveness and mercy are far better than whatever wealth those who stay behind accumulate." He means: and if you are killed in the way of Allah or die, then Allah will surely forgive you and have mercy on you, and that is better than what they amass of the world. Allah began with "and if you die or are killed," omitting the answer to the if, because that statement carries the meaning of an answer, a promise in the form of information. Some grammarians said it is as if He said: and if you die or are killed, then that is a mercy and forgiveness from Allah, since it came to pass in My way, better than what you amass.

phrases.translation: Whether you die or are martyred—all of you will be gathered before Allah
phrases.explanation: "Whether you die or are martyred, all of you will be gathered before Allah."  He means: and if you die or are killed, O believers, then with Allah is your return and gathering-place, and He will requite you according to your deeds. Therefore prefer that which brings you nearer to Allah and makes His good pleasure incumbent upon you, and brings you nearer to the Garden, namely jihad in the path of Allah and obedience to Him, over inclining toward the worldly life and its perishable trifles, which do not remain for you but vanish, and over abandoning obedience to Allah and the jihad. For that distances you from your Lord, makes His displeasure incumbent upon you, and brings you nearer to the Fire.

phrases.translation: It is out of Allah’s mercy that you ˹O Prophet˺ have been lenient with them. Had you been cruel or hard-hearted, they would have certainly abandoned you. So pardon them, ask Allah’s forgiveness for them, and consult with them in ˹conducting˺ matters. Once you make a decision, put your trust in Allah. Surely Allah loves those who trust in Him
phrases.explanation: "It is out of Allah's mercy that you have been lenient with them. Had you been cruel or hard-hearted, they would have certainly abandoned you. So pardon them, ask Allah's forgiveness for them, and consult with them in conducting matters. Once you make a decision, put your trust in Allah. Surely Allah loves those who trust in Him." "By a mercy from Allah you were gentle toward them": the particle is a connective, as the Arabs place it with the definite and the indefinite alike. "Had you been harsh and hard of heart, they would have dispersed": harsh means the rough one, hard of heart the one without mercy, and such was not his character, Allah having described him as compassionate and merciful to the believers. By Allah's mercy toward you and your believing companions you were gentle toward them, you bore the harm of whoever harmed you and forgave the wrongdoer. "So pardon them, ask forgiveness for them, and consult them": overlook what befell you of harm and beseech your Lord for them. The exegetes differed over the matter of consultation: some said the stratagems of war, to win hearts over, others that the correct opinion might become clear, others that the believers after him might follow his example and consult one another, as Allah praised the faithful in consultation among them. The most correct is that he was to consult his companions in what burdened him of the matter of his enemy, while Allah made known the import of matters to him through revelation, and when the community consults in sincerity, Allah guides them to the correct. "Once you make a decision, put your trust in Allah" means when your decision is firm, carry out what He commanded whether it agrees with your companions' advice or not, trusting your Lord and being content with His decree, and "Allah loves those who trust in Him" means those content with His decree and submitting to His judgment.

phrases.translation: If Allah helps you, none can defeat you. But if He denies you help, then who else can help you? So in Allah let the believers put their trust
phrases.explanation: "If Allah helps you, none can defeat you. But if He denies you help, then who else can help you? So in Allah let the believers put their trust." He means: if Allah helps you, O believers, against your enemies, then no one can overcome you, even if all creatures on earth gathered against you, so do not fear them because of your small number so long as you observe His command, for victory is for you. "If He forsakes you, then who could help you after Him" means if your Lord forsakes you for your transgression, you will find no helper, so do not abandon His command, lest you perish. "Upon Allah let the believers rely" means rely on your Lord, not on other creatures, submit to His decree, and fight in His way.

phrases.translation: It is not appropriate for a prophet to illegally withhold spoils of war. And whoever does so, it will be held against them on the Day of Judgment. Then every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and none will be wronged
phrases.explanation: "It is not appropriate for a prophet to illegally withhold spoils of war. And whoever does so, it will be held against them on the Day of Judgment. Then every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and none will be wronged."  The reciters differed over "it does not befit a prophet to be unfaithful": a group of the Hijaz and Iraq read it with the meaning that he should not be unfaithful to his companions concerning the spoils allotted to them, some adding that the verse came down over a cloak missing from the spoils at Badr, after which some said perhaps the Messenger took it, others over vanguard detachments to whom the Prophet allotted nothing, and still others that it instructs that he conceals nothing of the revelation. Others read it so that his companions should not be unfaithful to him, others that he should not be accused of unfaithfulness. The majority of Medina and Kufa read it with the other vocalization, and they too differed: some said it does not befit a prophet that his companions be unfaithful to him, the companions being omitted, others that he not be accused of unfaithfulness. The more correct reading is that unfaithfulness is not among the attributes of the prophets, and whoever is unfaithful is not a prophet, because Allah followed this statement with His threat that whoever is unfaithful shall bring what he was unfaithful in on the Day of Resurrection, which proves He forbade only unfaithfulness, a great crime the prophets do not commit, and commanded His servants to follow the path of their prophet.  "And whoever is unfaithful shall bring that in which he was unfaithful on the Day of Resurrection" is a threat to whoever misappropriates spoils, and it proves He forbade only unfaithfulness, a great crime the prophets do not commit. "Then every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and none will be wronged" means Allah requites every soul in full according to its deeds, wronging no one, for He is the One who pays every soul what it earned, whether obedience or disobedience, and He does not wrong anyone in the slightest.

phrases.translation: Are those who seek Allah’s pleasure like those who deserve Allah’s wrath? Hell is their home. What an evil destination
phrases.explanation: "Are those who seek Allah's pleasure like those who deserve Allah's wrath? Hell is their home. What an evil destination." The exegetes differed: some said it means he who pursues Allah's pleasure by abstaining from misappropriation like him who brought the wrath by misappropriating, others more generally. The most fitting is that after Allah's threat concerning misappropriation He asked: is he who obeys Allah in what He commanded and forbade equal to him who disobeys? They are not equal: whoever obeys has the Garden, whoever disobeys has the Fire. "He who pursues the pleasure of Allah" is he who abstained from misappropriation and acted in obedience, "like him who brought upon himself the wrath" means like him who turned away bearing Allah's wrath, meriting Hell, for they are not equal. "Evil is the final destination" means evil is the destination of him who brought upon himself the wrath, namely Hell.

phrases.translation: They ˹each˺ have varying degrees in the sight of Allah. And Allah is All-Seeing of what they do
phrases.explanation: "They each have varying degrees in the sight of Allah. And Allah is All-Seeing of what they do."  He means that he who pursues the good pleasure of Allah and he who has brought upon himself the wrath of Allah occupy differing ranks with Allah. For him who pursues Allah's pleasure there is honorable treatment and abundant reward, and for him who has brought upon himself the wrath there is humiliation and painful punishment. Others said the ranks are honorable dwelling-places with Allah for him who pursues His pleasure. "And Allah is All-Seeing of what they do" means Allah knows what the obedient and the disobedient perform, nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him, and He reckons the deeds of both until every soul is fully requited for its good and evil.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah has done the believers a ˹great˺ favour by raising a messenger from among them—reciting to them His revelations, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom. For indeed they had previously been clearly astray
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, Allah has done the believers a great favour by raising a messenger from among them, reciting to them His revelations, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom. For indeed they had previously been clearly astray." He means: Allah conferred a favor when He sent the believers a messenger from among themselves, of their own tongue, so they would understand. "Reciting His signs" means he recites the verses of His Book, "purifies them" means He cleanses them of sins through their obeying him, and "teaches them the Book and the wisdom" means the Book and its interpretation, the wisdom being the sunna Allah established through the Messenger's tongue and his clarification of it. "Before that they were in manifest error" means they were in dense ignorance, knowing no truth and rejecting no falsehood.

phrases.translation: Why is it when you suffered casualties ˹at Uḥud˺—although you had made your enemy suffer twice as much ˹at Badr˺—you protested, “How could this be?”? Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “It is because of your disobedience.” Surely Allah is Most Capable of everything
phrases.explanation: "Why is it when you suffered casualties at Uhud, although you had made your enemy suffer twice as much at Badr, you protested, 'How could this be?' Say, 'It is because of your disobedience.' Surely Allah is Most Capable of everything." He means: when a calamity struck you, O believers, the slain and wounded at Uhud, while you had inflicted twice as much on them at Badr, killing seventy and taking seventy captive, you asked from where this came. "Say: it comes from yourselves" means it struck you through your transgression of His command. "Allah is capable of all things" means possessor of power. The exegetes differed over "from yourselves": some said through your opposing the Prophet when he advised staying in the city, others through your taking captives at Badr and accepting ransom.

phrases.translation: So what you suffered on the day the two armies met was by Allah’s Will, so that He might distinguish the ˹true˺ believers
phrases.explanation: "So what you suffered on the day the two armies met was by Allah's Will, so that He might distinguish the true believers."  He means: what struck you on the day the two hosts met, the day of Uhud when the host of the Muslims and the polytheists met, and what struck them was the slaying of their killed and the wounds of their wounded, came to pass by Allah's permission, that is, by His decree and predetermination.
