"And that He might know the believers" means so that the people of faith might distinguish the believers from the hypocrites and recognize them, so that the affair of the two groups would not remain hidden. The explanation of "that He might know the believers" was given earlier.

phrases.translation: and expose the hypocrites. When it was said to them, “Come fight in the cause of Allah or ˹at least˺ defend yourselves,” they replied, “If we had known there was fighting, we would have definitely gone with you.” They were closer to disbelief than to belief on that day—for saying with their mouths what was not in their hearts. Allah is All-Knowing of what they hide
phrases.explanation: "And expose the hypocrites. When it was said to them, 'Come fight in the cause of Allah or at least defend yourselves,' they replied, 'If we had known there was fighting, we would have definitely gone with you.'" They were closer to disbelief than to belief that day, saying with their mouths what was not in their hearts. "Allah is All-Knowing of what they hide." He means a hypocrite leader and companions who turned away when the Prophet marched out at Uhud. The Muslims said: come fight with us, or repel the enemy with your numbers, and they said: if we knew you would fight we would march out, but no battle will take place, disclosing more than they concealed. "Allah knows what they conceal" means He knows their enmity, consigning them to the Fire.

phrases.translation: Those who sat at home, saying about their brothers, “Had they listened to us, they would not have been killed.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Try not to die if what you say is true!”
phrases.explanation: "Those who sat at home, saying about their brothers, 'Had they listened to us, they would not have been killed.' Say, 'Try not to die if what you say is true.'" He means: those who said of their brethren killed at Uhud, their fellow tribesmen, while they sat at home and refrained from the jihad. "Had they obeyed us, they would not have been killed." So He told His Prophet to say: "ward off death from yourselves, if you are truthful," that is, if had our brethren stayed home they would not have been killed, then ward off death from yourselves, for you sat back and will inevitably die. "Those" stands in the accusative as a substitution for "those who acted hypocritically," though the nominative is also possible.

phrases.translation: Never think of those martyred in the cause of Allah as dead. In fact, they are alive with their Lord, well provided for—
phrases.explanation: "Never think of those martyred in the cause of Allah as dead. In fact, they are alive with their Lord, well provided for, rejoicing in Allah's bounties and being delighted for those yet to join them. There will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve." "Do not think" means do not suppose. "Those killed in the way of Allah" means the companions of the Messenger killed at Uhud. Do not deem them dead, perceiving nothing and tasting no blessings, for they are alive with Me, enjoying My provision and rejoicing over the honor, bounty, and reward I have bestowed. The grammarians gave two views on the accusative of "rejoicing": as a circumstantial qualifier from "with their Lord," or from "they are provided for," and the nominative would also be permissible.

phrases.translation: rejoicing in Allah’s bounties and being delighted for those yet to join them. There will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve
phrases.explanation: "Rejoicing in Allah's bounties and being delighted for those yet to join them. There will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve." This refers to the martyrs of Uhud: alive with their Lord, enjoying His provision, they rejoice over their brothers who have not yet joined them, those left behind alive upon the path of jihad, knowing that should these fall as martyrs they will attain the same honor. So they rejoice that for them there shall be no fear, being safe from Allah's punishment and certain of His good pleasure, and no grief over worldly matters, on account of the repose and nearness to Allah they have attained. "An la" is accusative with the meaning: they rejoice because there shall be no fear upon them nor grief.

phrases.translation: They are joyful for receiving Allah’s grace and bounty, and that Allah does not deny the reward of the believers
phrases.explanation: "They are joyful for receiving Allah's grace and bounty, and that Allah does not deny the reward of the believers." "They rejoice" means they are gladdened at a favor from Allah, the honor He bestows when they come before Him, and at a bounty He lavishes for their past obedience and struggle against His enemies, "and that Allah does not let the reward go to waste" meaning He does not nullify the recompense for whoever held His Messenger to be true and followed him. The reciters differed: some read "and that Allah" with a fatha connected to the rejoicing, others with a kasra as a new beginning. The most correct is the fatha, by the consensus of the authoritative reciters.

phrases.translation: ˹As for˺ those who responded to the call of Allah and His Messenger after their injury, those of them who did good and were mindful ˹of Allah˺ will have a great reward
phrases.explanation: "As for those who responded to the call of Allah and His Messenger after their injury, those of them who did good and were mindful of Allah will have a great reward." He means: "and that Allah does not let the reward of the believers go to waste," namely of those who responded after the wound afflicted them. In particular those who followed the Messenger to Hamra al-Asad in pursuit of the enemy, the enemy leader and polytheists with him after their retreat from Uhud, for the Messenger pursued them eight miles from Medina, so all would see he still had strength. Thus He promised the one who did good among them, when he fears Allah and obeys Him for the rest of his life, "a great reward," the abundant recompense for his good deeds.

phrases.translation: Those who were warned, “Your enemies have mobilized their forces against you, so fear them,” the warning only made them grow stronger in faith and they replied, “Allah ˹alone˺ is sufficient ˹as an aid˺ for us and ˹He˺ is the best Protector.”
phrases.explanation: "Those who were warned, 'Your enemies have mobilized their forces against you, so fear them,' the warning only made them grow stronger in faith and they replied, 'Allah alone is sufficient as an aid for us and He is the best Protector.'" He means: "and that Allah does not let the reward of the believers go to waste", those to whom the people said the people have gathered against you. The first "people" are a group asked by the enemy leader to discourage the Messenger and his companions, who had set out after him from Uhud to Hamra al-Asad, and the second are the enemy leader and his companions of Quraysh from Uhud. "They have gathered against you" means they have brought men to meet you and return against you in battle. "So fear them" means be on your guard, for you are no match for them. But it only increased them in faith, adding conviction to their affirmation of Allah, His promise, and His Messenger's promise, and they marched on until they attained Allah's good pleasure, saying out of trust in Allah: "Allah is sufficient for us, and what an excellent Guardian is He." The Guardian is the one entrusted with managing another's affair, and since they committed their affair to Allah, He described Himself as their excellent Guardian. The exegetes differed over when the warning was given: some said on the expedition from Uhud to Hamra al-Asad, others at the lesser Badr expedition the year after Uhud.

phrases.translation: So they returned with Allah’s favours and grace, suffering no harm. For they sought to please Allah. And surely Allah is ˹the˺ Lord of infinite bounty
phrases.explanation: "So they returned with Allah's favours and grace, suffering no harm. For they sought to please Allah. And surely Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty." He means: those who responded after the wound afflicted them turned back from their pursuit of the enemy to Hamra al-Asad "with a favor from Allah," well-being from their Lord, encountering no enemy, "and a bounty," the profits of their trade and the reward they acquired. "No harm touched them" means nothing disagreeable from their enemy befell them. "They followed the good pleasure of Allah" by obeying His Messenger in pursuing the enemy's trail. "Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty" means the Possessor of beneficence, turning away their enemy who had resolved to attack again, tremendous for the creature upon whom He bestows it.

phrases.translation: That ˹warning˺ was only ˹from˺ Satan, trying to prompt you to fear his followers. So do not fear them; fear Me if you are ˹true˺ believers
phrases.explanation: "That warning was only from Satan, trying to prompt you to fear his followers. So do not fear them, fear Me if you are true believers." He means: the one who said to you, O believers, "the people have gathered against you," instilling fear in you through the multitudes of your enemy advancing toward you, acted by a deed of Satan cast upon the mouths of those who said it. He instills fear in you through his allies among the polytheists, the enemy leader and his companions of Quraysh, so that you fear them and turn cowardly. Others said: that is only Satan who magnifies the affair of the polytheists in your souls, O hypocrites, so that you fear him. On the grammar of "instills fear of his allies": it means he instills fear in you through his allies, just as "warn of a severe might" means warn you of His might. Therefore do not fear them, but fear Allah if you are believers.

phrases.translation: ˹O Prophet!˺ Do not grieve for those who race to disbelieve—surely they will not harm Allah in the least. It is Allah’s Will to disallow them a share in the Hereafter, and they will suffer a tremendous punishment
phrases.explanation: "O Prophet! Do not grieve for those who race to disbelief, surely they will not harm Allah in the least. It is Allah's Will to disallow them a share in the Hereafter, and they will suffer a tremendous punishment." Let not the disbelief grieve you, O Prophet, of those who hasten into disbelief while turning back on their heels, the people of hypocrisy. They will not harm Allah by hastening into disbelief, and just as haste toward faith would be of no benefit to Him, so haste toward disbelief is of no harm to Him. "Allah wills not to assign them any portion in the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment" means He wills to deprive them of the bliss of the Hereafter and make their recompense a great punishment in the Fire.

phrases.translation: Those who trade belief for disbelief will never harm Allah in the least, and they will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: "Those who trade belief for disbelief will never harm Allah in the least, and they will suffer a painful punishment." By this He means the hypocrites, about whom He told His Prophet their haste toward unbelief should not grieve him. These purchased unbelief in exchange for faith, apostatizing after entering it. They will not harm Allah by their unbelief, on the contrary they harm only themselves, making a punishment from Allah obligatory which they cannot bear. With these verses, from "what struck you on the day the two hosts met was by the leave of Allah" to this verse, Allah urged His servants to keep conviction pure, turn wholly to Him, and be content with Him alone as Helper, encouraging jihad: whomever He assists is never forsaken, whomever He forsakes is not helped.

phrases.translation: Those who disbelieve should not think that living longer is good for them. They are only given more time to increase in sin, and they will suffer a humiliating punishment
phrases.explanation: "Those who disbelieve should not think that living longer is good for them. They are only given more time to increase in sin, and they will suffer a humiliating punishment." Let not those who disbelieve in Allah, His Messenger, and what he brought think that Our granting them respite is better for themselves. "Respite" means the prolonging of the lifespan and the deferring of the term of death, as in "leave me for a long time." We grant them respite only that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment. The reciters differed: some read "let not those who disbelieve think" with the third person, others with the second person addressed to the Prophet, meaning do not think, O Prophet, that Our granting respite to the disbelievers is better for them.

phrases.translation: Allah would not leave the believers in the condition you were in, until He distinguished the good from the evil ˹among you˺. Nor would Allah ˹directly˺ reveal to you the unseen, but He chooses whoever He wills as a messenger. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And if you are faithful and mindful ˹of Allah˺, you will receive a great reward
phrases.explanation: "Allah would not leave the believers in the condition you were in, until He distinguished the good from the evil among you. Nor would Allah directly reveal to you the unseen, but He chooses whoever He wills as a messenger. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And if you are faithful and mindful of Allah, you will receive a great reward." "Allah will not leave the believers in the state in which you are" means the intermingling of believer with hypocrite so neither is distinguished from the other, "until He distinguishes the evil from the good" means until He distinguishes the hypocrite who conceals unbelief from the sincere believer, through trials and testing, just as He distinguished them on the Day of Uhud. The exegetes differed over "the evil": some said as above, others that He distinguishes believer from unbeliever through emigration and jihad, and the first is more fitting because the surrounding verses concern the hypocrites. "Nor would Allah give you insight into the unseen" means He would not give you knowledge of the inner states of hearts, to know believer from hypocrite and unbeliever, but He distinguishes them through trials, as at Uhud, and through jihad, except that He chooses from His messengers whom He wills and gives him insight into part of what is hidden, revealing it through his message. Believe in Allah and His messengers, and if you are faithful and mindful you will receive a great reward.

phrases.translation: And do not let those who ˹greedily˺ withhold Allah’s bounties think it is good for them—in fact, it is bad for them! They will be leashed ˹by their necks˺ on the Day of Judgment with whatever ˹wealth˺ they used to withhold. And Allah is the ˹sole˺ inheritor of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do
phrases.explanation: "And do not let those who greedily withhold Allah's bounties think it is good for them. In fact, it is bad for them! They will be leashed by their necks on the Day of Judgment with whatever wealth they used to withhold. And Allah is the sole inheritor of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do." "Nay, it is worse for them" means withholding brings them evil and harm in this world and the next, for the withholder is threatened with punishment. The reciters differed: a group of the people of Hijaz and Iraq read "let not those who withhold" with the second person, another group with the third person, and the people of Arabic differed in explanation. The second person reading is more correct because "think" requires a subject and a predicate, and "those who withhold" supplies the subject with "that it is good for them" as predicate, running along the well-known path of eloquent Arabic, even though the third person reading is not incorrect but not the most eloquent. By "withholding" here is meant withholding the zakah, as is clear from the abundant reports of the Messenger that what was withheld will be hung around the neck on the Day of Resurrection, and from the following verse where the polytheists among the Jews, when commanded the zakah, claimed Allah is poor and they are rich. Others said it meant the Jews who were miserly in expounding to people what Allah sent down in the Torah about the Prophet and his description, concealing it. "It will be hung around their necks" means Allah will make what they withheld of the zakah into a collar around their necks in the form of well-known collars. Others said a collar of fire is placed around their necks, others that the Jewish rabbis who concealed his prophethood will carry what they concealed, others that they will be made to come on the Day of Resurrection with the very wealth they withheld in this world. "To Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth" means all of it returns to Him, nothing remains with its possessor, and whoever dies, his wealth passes to his heirs yet all of it belongs to Allah, "and Allah is All-Aware of what you do."

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah has heard those ˹among the Jews˺ who said, “Allah is poor; we are rich!” We have certainly recorded their slurs and their killing of prophets unjustly. Then We will say, “Taste the torment of burning
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, Allah has heard those among the Jews who said, 'Allah is poor, we are rich!' We have certainly recorded their slurs and their killing of prophets unjustly. Then We will say, 'Taste the torment of burning.'" This verse and those after it were revealed concerning some of the Jews who lived in the time of the Messenger. Allah has heard the saying of those of the Jews who said: "Truly, Allah is poor toward us, and we are rich in relation to Him." We shall write down what they said of falsehood and fabrication against their Lord, and their killing of their prophets without right. The reciters differed over "We shall write down what they said, and their killing": the reciters of Hijaz and most of Iraq read it with the first person and the accusative, while some Kufan reciters read the passive with the third person and the nominative. The correct reading is the first person with the accusative, to agree with "and We shall say," for the two are joined, and mixing active and passive without a compelling reason falls outside eloquent Arabic. "Then We will say, Taste the torment of burning" is said to them on the Day of Resurrection.

phrases.translation: This is ˹the reward˺ for what your hands have done. And Allah is never unjust to ˹His˺ creation.”
phrases.explanation: "This is the reward for what your hands have done. And Allah is never unjust to His creation." That is: our statement on the Day of Resurrection, "Taste the punishment of the burning," is because of what your hands sent forth and earned in this world. Allah is just and does no wrong, so He would not punish a servant without that servant deserving it, but He requites every soul according to what it has earned. Thus He requited those Jews, who said Allah is poor and killed the prophets without right, with the burning because of the sins they earned and the lies they invented about Allah after the warning reached them. He is unjust to none of His creatures, but the Just among them.

phrases.translation: Those ˹are the same people˺ who say, “Allah has commanded us not to believe in any messenger unless he brings us an offering to be consumed by fire ˹from the sky˺.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Other prophets did in fact come to you before me with clear proofs and ˹even˺ what you demanded—why then did you kill them, if what you say is true?”
phrases.explanation: "Those are the same people who say, 'Allah has commanded us not to believe in any messenger unless he brings us an offering to be consumed by fire from the sky.' Say, O Prophet, 'Other prophets did in fact come to you before me with clear proofs and even what you demanded. Why then did you kill them, if what you say is true?'" "Allah has charged us not to believe until he brings an offering the fire consumes" means He enjoined not to hold any messenger truthful until he brings a sacrifice whose being consumed proves his truthfulness. Allah tells His Prophet to say: messengers before me came with the clear proofs and what you claimed would oblige you to believe, so why did you kill them, if you are truthful?

phrases.translation: If you are rejected by them, so too were messengers before you who came with clear proofs, divine Books, and enlightening Scriptures
phrases.explanation: "If you are rejected by them, so too were messengers before you who came with clear proofs, divine Books, and enlightening Scriptures." This is a consolation from Allah to His Prophet concerning the harm done him by the Jews and the polytheists. Let not their saying "Allah is poor" or their denial of you grieve you, for their forefathers denied messengers before you who came with arguments that cut off all excuse and signs that render creation powerless, and those are the clear proofs. "The scriptures" is the plural of book. "The Book" means the Torah and the Gospel, because the Jews denied the son of Mary and distorted what Moses brought about the Prophet. "The illuminating" means that which illuminates and makes the truth clear, derived from light.

phrases.translation: Every soul will taste death. And you will only receive your full reward on the Day of Judgment. Whoever is spared from the Fire and is admitted into Paradise will ˹indeed˺ triumph, whereas the life of this world is no more than the delusion of enjoyment
phrases.explanation: "Every soul will taste death. And you will only receive your full reward on the Day of Judgment. Whoever is spared from the Fire and is admitted into Paradise will indeed triumph, whereas the life of this world is no more than the delusion of enjoyment." Whoever is kept away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has truly escaped and attained the great honor. "The worldly life is nothing but a deceptive enjoyment" means the enjoyments of the world let you take pleasure by delusion, with no reality at the trial: afterward it turns against you with calamities, so do not rely upon it. One exegete read "delusion" as meager enjoyment, but the correct view is that delusion is deception in Arabic, naming the deluding Satan who deludes the son of Adam into disobedience.

phrases.translation: You ˹believers˺ will surely be tested in your wealth and yourselves, and you will certainly hear many hurtful words from those who were given the Scripture before you and ˹from˺ the polytheists. But if you are patient and mindful ˹of Allah˺—surely this is a resolve to aspire to
phrases.explanation: "You believers will surely be tested in your wealth and yourselves, and you will certainly hear many hurtful words from those who were given the Scripture before you and from the polytheists. But if you are patient and mindful of Allah, surely this is a resolve to aspire to." You will be tested in your possessions, yourselves, and by hurtful words from the People of the Book and the polytheists. It was said this was revealed concerning a Jewish chief of one of the Jewish tribes, and others said concerning a poet of the polytheists who reviled the Messenger in lampoons. "If you are patient and mindful of Allah," enduring the hurt, "that belongs to the matters of firm resolve," which Allah has urged His servants to hold fast to.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember, O Prophet,˺ when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture to make it known to people and not hide it, yet they cast it behind their backs and traded it for a fleeting gain. What a miserable profit
phrases.explanation: "Remember, O Prophet, when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture to make it known to people and not hide it, yet they cast it behind their backs and traded it for a fleeting gain. What a miserable profit." He means the affair of these Jews and the People of the Book, when Allah took their covenant that they would make your affair clear in their Book, the Torah and the Gospel, that you are truly a messenger sent with the truth. They broke His covenant, concealed your affair, called you a liar, and took a contemptible compensation of worldly goods for it, and how evil is that which they buy. The exegetes differed: some said the Jews specifically, others everyone given knowledge of religion.

phrases.translation: Do not let those who rejoice in their misdeeds and love to take credit for what they have not done think they will escape torment. They will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: "Do not let those who rejoice in their misdeeds and love to take credit for what they have not done think they will escape torment. They will suffer a painful punishment." The exegetes differed over whom this means. Some said a group of the hypocrites who stayed behind when the Messenger fought the enemy, and when he returned excused themselves and loved to be praised for what they had not done. Others said a group of the Jewish scribes who rejoiced in leading the people astray and in the people attributing knowledge to them. Others said a group of Jews who rejoiced in their unanimous denial of the Prophet and loved to be praised as people of prayer and fasting. Others said it means those who rejoiced in altering Allah's Book and loved the people to praise them for it. Others said they rejoiced in what Allah had bestowed upon the family of Abraham, peace be upon him. And others said it was those who rejoiced in their wrongdoing and loved praise for deeds they did not perform. Whatever the referent, do not think them in safety from the punishment, for them there is a painful punishment, and no praise they seek will avail them on that day, so fear Allah and turn to Him in repentance before the torment overtakes you and there is no helper for them.

phrases.translation: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Most Capable of everything
phrases.explanation: "To Allah alone belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Most Capable of everything." This is a refutation from Allah of those who said: "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich." He says: to Allah belongs the sovereignty over everything the heavens and the earth contain. How then, O you who fabricate lies against Allah, can the One to whom that sovereignty belongs be poor? He is able to hasten the punishment for those who said that and for every denier and fabricator of lies against Him, but out of grace He has shown forbearance toward His creatures. Therefore He said: "and Allah has power over all things," over the destruction of those who said that and the hastening of His punishment upon them.

phrases.translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the day and night there are signs for people of reason
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the day and night there are signs for people of reason." This is an argument from Allah against whoever said He is poor, showing that He governs and disposes of affairs, and that enriching and impoverishing lie in His hand. He says: reflect and take instruction, for in what He created of the heavens and the earth for your sustenance, and in the night and day succeeding one another for your benefit, there are signs. Whoever has understanding knows that whoever attributes poverty to Him while He is rich is a liar, for all of that lies in His hand: He disposes of it, and were He to remove it you would perish. Take instruction, O people of understanding.

phrases.translation: ˹They are˺ those who remember Allah while standing, sitting, and lying on their sides, and reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth ˹and pray˺, “Our Lord! You have not created ˹all of˺ this without purpose. Glory be to You! Protect us from the torment of the Fire
phrases.explanation: "They are those who remember Allah while standing, sitting, and lying on their sides, and reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth and pray, 'Our Lord! You have not created all of this without purpose. Glory be to You! Protect us from the torment of the Fire.'" "Those who remember Allah while standing and sitting" belongs to the description of people of understanding, "those who" referring back to them. The meaning is: signs for people of understanding, who remember Allah while standing, meaning in their prayer, sitting in their Tashahhud and outside prayer, and lying on their sides, sleeping, since "on their sides" means lying down. "Reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth" means they take a lesson from the handiwork of its Maker, knowing that none can make this except He whom nothing resembles, the Sovereign, Provider, and Creator in whose hand lie enrichment and impoverishment, life and death, misery and felicity. "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain" declares His transcendence from purposeless creation, and "Protect us from the punishment of the Fire" is their supplication.

phrases.translation: Our Lord! Indeed, those You commit to the Fire will be ˹completely˺ disgraced! And the wrongdoers will have no helpers
phrases.explanation: "Our Lord! Indeed, those You commit to the Fire will be completely disgraced! And the wrongdoers will have no helpers." The exegetes differed over this. Some said: whoever You admit to the Fire to abide eternally, him You have disgraced, but a believer whose final abode is Paradise is not disgraced even if punished in the Fire for a time. Others said: whoever You admit to the Fire, whether eternally or not, has already been disgraced by the punishment. The correct view is that whoever is admitted to the Fire has been disgraced by entering it, even if taken out again, because disgrace is humiliation. "And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers" means for whoever transgresses Allah's command there is no helper against Allah to avert His punishment from him.

phrases.translation: Our Lord! We have heard the caller to ˹true˺ belief, ˹proclaiming,˺ ‘Believe in your Lord ˹alone˺,’ so we believed. Our Lord! Forgive our sins, absolve us of our misdeeds, and allow us ˹each˺ to die as one of the virtuous
phrases.explanation: "Our Lord! We have heard the caller to true belief, proclaiming, 'Believe in your Lord alone,' so we believed. Our Lord! Forgive our sins, absolve us of our misdeeds, and allow us each to die as one of the virtuous." The exegetes differed over "the caller": some said it is the Quran itself calling to faith, others said it is the Prophet proclaiming the message. They pray: forgive us our sins, wipe away our evil deeds, and cause us to die with the righteous, that is, as believers submitting to Allah, for dying with the righteous is an honor and a protection from the Fire, and no one is admitted to it except by His mercy.

phrases.translation: Our Lord! Grant us what You have promised us through Your messengers and do not put us to shame on Judgment Day—for certainly You never fail in Your promise.”
phrases.explanation: "Our Lord! Grant us what You have promised us through Your messengers and do not put us to shame on Judgment Day, for certainly You never fail in Your promise." Some theologians said this is a request in form but an assertion in meaning, since they knew Allah does not break His promise and grants what He promised out of grace. Others said it is a genuine supplication to be counted among those granted the promised honorable treatment. Others said they longed for Allah to hasten His promised victory over their enemies. The view nearest to correct is that this describes those who emigrated and were persecuted and who longed for Allah to hasten their victory, and this is confirmed by the following verse about those who emigrated and fought.

phrases.translation: So their Lord responded to them: “I will never deny any of you—male or female—the reward of your deeds. Both are equal in reward. Those who migrated or were expelled from their homes, and were persecuted for My sake and fought and ˹some˺ were martyred—I will certainly forgive their sins and admit them into Gardens under which rivers flow, as a reward from Allah. And with Allah is the finest reward!”
phrases.explanation: "So their Lord responded to them: 'I will never deny any of you, male or female, the reward of your deeds. Both are equal in reward. Those who migrated or were expelled from their homes, and were persecuted for My sake and fought and some were martyred, I will certainly forgive their sins and admit them into Gardens under which rivers flow, as a reward from Allah. And with Allah is the finest reward!'" Their Lord answered the supplicants: I do not let the work of any worker among you go to waste, whoever does good, whether man or woman. It was reported that someone asked the Messenger why the men are mentioned but not the women in connection with the emigration, so Allah sent down this verse about it. "You are of one another" means you believers are of one another in mutual support, the community of faith, and My ruling concerning all of you is equal. "Those who migrated" means those who left their people of unbelief for Allah and emigrated to their brethren of faith, "and were driven out of their dwellings" refers to the emigrants whom the polytheists of Quraysh drove from their homes in Mecca, "and were harmed on My way" means whoever was harmed for obedience, "and fought and were killed" upon that way. "I shall wipe out their evil deeds" means I shall pardon them with My forgiveness, "and admit them into gardens under which rivers flow, as a reward from Allah," recompense for what they endured, "and with Allah is the finest reward," which no eye has seen and no ear has heard. The reciters differed over "fought and were killed": some read without doubling, some with doubling.

phrases.translation: Do not be deceived by the prosperity of the disbelievers throughout the land
phrases.explanation: "Do not be deceived by the prosperity of the disbelievers throughout the land." "Let it not deceive you" means their roaming about and travelling in the land, their prosperity and bustling trade in it. Allah forbade His Prophet to be deceived by their travelling and by His reprieve to them despite their polytheism, their denial of His favors, and their worship of other than Him. The address is directed to the Prophet while his followers and companions are intended, for he proclaimed and called to the truth by Allah's command, and the believers should take heed of their example and not be deluded by the worldly success of the disbelievers, since it is only a deception that will soon end in their ruin.

phrases.translation: It is only a brief enjoyment. Then Hell will be their home—what an evil place to rest
phrases.explanation: "It is only a brief enjoyment. Then Hell will be their home, what an evil place to rest." "A meager enjoyment" means their moving to and fro through the lands and their bustling activity therein is an enjoyment they take pleasure in for a short time, until their appointed terms of life and the hours of their death seize them away. "Then their abode is Hell" after their death, "the abode" being the destination toward which they betake themselves on the Day of Resurrection and into which they come to rest. And "what a wretched resting place" means what a wretched bed and couch Hell is, with its torment and humiliation for whoever enters it.

phrases.translation: But those who are mindful of their Lord will be in Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there forever—as an accommodation from Allah. And what is with Allah is best for the virtuous
phrases.explanation: "But those who are mindful of their Lord will be in Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there forever, as an accommodation from Allah. And what is with Allah is best for the virtuous." "But those who fear their Lord" means those who fear Allah by obeying Him and seeking His good pleasure. "For them there are gardens under which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally." "As a welcome from Allah" is a lodging He bestows, part of the honor He grants them. "And what is with Allah is better for the virtuous" means what is with Allah of honor and good return is better for the righteous than the perishable enjoyment in which the disbelievers move about, for what is with Allah for the people of His obedience is abiding and never passes away.

phrases.translation: Indeed, there are some among the People of the Book who truly believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you ˹believers˺ and what was revealed to them. They humble themselves before Allah—never trading Allah’s revelations for a fleeting gain. Their reward is with their Lord. Surely Allah is swift in reckoning
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, there are some among the People of the Book who truly believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you believers and what was revealed to them. They humble themselves before Allah, never trading Allah's revelations for a fleeting gain. Their reward is with their Lord. Surely Allah is swift in reckoning." The exegetes differed over who is meant: some said the Christian king of Abyssinia and his companions, others said a Jewish convert and those with him, others said the converted People of the Book generally, and the correct view is the general one, since "the People of the Book" covers both Jews and Christians. "Those who believe in Allah" acknowledge His oneness and believe "in what has been sent down to you" and "to them," the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms, "humbly submitting" through obedience. "They do not sell the signs of Allah for a paltry price" means they do not falsify the description of the Prophet in their books for a worthless gain, but conform to the truth. "For them is their reward with their Lord," stored with Him until the Day of Resurrection when He repays it in full. "Allah is swift in the reckoning" because nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him, so there is no delay.

phrases.translation: O believers! Patiently endure, persevere, stand on guard, and be mindful of Allah, so you may be successful
phrases.explanation: "O believers! Patiently endure, persevere, stand on guard, and be mindful of Allah, so you may be successful." The exegetes differed over the explanation. Some said: be patient concerning your religion, be more steadfast than the disbelievers, and keep guard against them. Others said: be patient concerning your religion, be steadfast in awaiting My promise for your obedience to Me, and keep guard against your enemies. Others said: be patient concerning jihad, be more steadfast than your enemy, and keep guard against them. Others said "keep guard" means persevere in the prayers, awaiting one prayer after another. The most fitting view is this: "O you who believe" means O you who have held Allah and His Messenger to be true. "Be patient" means be patient concerning your religion and obedience to your Lord, for patience here covers all obedience to Allah in what He commanded and forbade, the heavy and difficult of it and the light and easy, so that you do not despair when hardship befalls you. "Be more steadfast" means be more steadfast than your enemies among the polytheists, because the reciprocal verb form in Arabic involves two parties, so the believers are commanded to outlast their enemies until Allah grants them victory over them, raises His word, and abases their enemies, so that their enemy will not be more patient than they. "And keep guard" means keep guard against your enemies and the enemies of your religion among the people of polytheism, in the path of Allah. The origin of the guard is the tethering of horses against the enemy, just as the enemy tethered his horses against them, and that was then applied to everyone who resides at a frontier outpost and defends those behind him against those who wish to harm them, whether he has horses tethered or is on foot with no mount. This is the known meaning of the guard in the usage of the people, and speech is directed toward the current known meaning unless something in the Book, a report from the Messenger, or a consensus of the exegetes indicates otherwise. "And fear Allah, so that you may succeed" means guard yourselves against opposing His command or anticipating His prohibition, so that you may succeed and thereby abide forever in bliss and attain with Him your desires. This verse closes the commentary on this surah, so hold fast to it, call others to it, act upon it in all your affairs, and ask Allah to make you among those who succeed, for success is only by His grace and guidance, and whoever He guides is truly successful.
